ahos_doctor.description: Is ahOS correctly set up, and what is missing? One read-only pass over credentials (set under which name, authenticates, right account), wiring (integration rows, dos pointers, surface_role_map, Notion options), what travels (registered skills match the repo) and outcomes (did the dos sweep close the days it should have). Each finding carries its exact fix; nothing is changed. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/ahos_doctor.md

families.description: Which check families to run: 'credentials' (present, authenticates, right account), 'wiring' (integration rows, dos pointers, surface_role_map, Notion options), 'travels' (registered skills match the repo receipts), 'outcomes' (routines produced what they should have: the dos sweep closed its days). Default: all four.

artifact_delete.description: Delete artifacts by id. Defaults to a reversible soft-delete that archives the row; search already excludes archived rows, and artifact_update restores them. `archive_only: false` is an irreversible hard delete that cascades to the artifact's entity and external links. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/artifact_delete.md

archive_only.description: Soft-delete (archive) instead of a hard row delete. Defaults to true — the safe path. Only pass false when a real, irreversible row delete is intended.

archived_reason.description: Optional human-readable reason recorded on archived_reason for the soft-delete path.

artifact_embed_backfill.description: Embed artifacts, entities and people that have no vector yet, so they become reachable by meaning rather than keywords. Embedding otherwise happens only at write time, so anything written while the embedding key was unset or out of credits stays permanently unsearchable until this runs. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/artifact_embed_backfill.md

batch_size.description: Rows fetched and embedded per round trip. Default 25.

max_batches.description: Cap on batches processed by THIS call — the budget that keeps one call bounded. Default 2 (so 50 rows). Raise it to drain faster, at the cost of a longer call.

dry_run.description: Count what would be embedded without calling OpenAI or writing anything. Use to size the backlog before spending credits. Defaults to false.

artifact_extract_text.description: Extract text from a captured PDF or image artifact into its searchable content. Run after capturing a file so it shows up in knowledge_search.

artifact_id.description: Artifact whose stored file should have its text extracted.

artifact_get.description: Fetch a single artifact's full content and its linked PARAMPS entities by id. For a discovered pointer it also prints the link, connector, external id, owner, content hash with its kind (md5 or modified_time) and the modified-at-source time.

id.description: Artifact id returned by capture or search.

artifact_get_file.description: artifact_get plus a resolvable reference to the artifact's original file, when one exists. Three outcomes: a real stored file returns a reference; a plain-text capture has no file and says so cleanly; a missing file is reported as missing rather than as an error. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/artifact_get_file.md

id.description: Artifact id returned by capture or search.

artifact_sync_entities.description: Resolve extracted entities against the entities table, create missing rows, and link all resolved entities back to the artifact in one idempotent pass.

artifact_id.description: Artifact id to attach entity links to.

id.description: Existing entity id, if already known.

entity_type.description: Entity type, e.g. people, organization, event, task, fact, signal.

id.description: Artifact id to update.

archived.description: Soft-archive flag. Set false to restore a soft-deleted artifact (clears the archive stamps); set true to archive.

Use brevo_list_tools to discover tool names and their input schemas; arguments are passed through verbatim and validated upstream by Brevo. Reads the event first so bad ids fail safely and the reply names what was cancelled; attendees are emailed by default. Parks for the owner's approval when the event has guests other than the owner. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/calendar_delete_event.md

event_id.description: Event id, from calendar_list_events. For a recurring series this is ONE OCCURRENCE and only that occurrence is deleted; to cancel a whole series, delete the id shown as its recurring series id.

Use 'none' only for an event nobody else is on, or a correction made seconds after the original.

Every returned event names the account it came from.

Full notes: docs/guides/tools/capability_get.md

name.description: Fetch a single capability by exact name (case-insensitive); strips optional 'ahos/' or 'ahkms/' namespace prefix and resolves ritual and skill aliases (sync/synth/dos, reflect/dos-reflect, prep/prep-day-unattended, groom-issues/unblock).

surface.description: Filter to capabilities available on this runtime surface.

client.description: Filter to capabilities available on this client.

scope.description: Filter by scope (global | personal | work | ahLtd).

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

include_archived.description: Include archived capabilities. Defaults to false.

include_body.description: Default true. false returns the header (kind, surface, clients, scope, storage, body_sha256, body_synced_at, updated_at) without the body, for freshness probes: about 1 KB instead of the whole skill.

capability_register.description: Register a capability — a skill, agent or command — in the registry, creating it or fully replacing it by name. Full replace, not merge: fields you omit are cleared, so send the whole capability every time. Skill bar & placement: capability_get({ name: 'writing-for-agents' }). Full notes: docs/guides/tools/capability_register.md

name.description: Capability name; unique per user (case-insensitive). Re-registering an existing name updates it (full replace).

description.description: Short summary of what the capability does.

kind.description: Capability kind(s): skill | agent | command (single or array for twins e.g. ['skill', 'agent']).

surface.description: Runtime execution surfaces: claude-code | claude-synced | api. Non-empty array.

clients.description: Informational client surfaces: chat | cowork | mobile | cursor | ide | terminal.

scope.description: Identity-context / binding scope: global | personal | work | ahLtd.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

storage_location.description: Canonical home. kms-db/kms-repo = hosted by the kms; claude/openai = indexed (external owner).

storage_url.description: Pointer to the canonical home (repo path / URL). Required unless storage_location='kms-db'; must be omitted for kms-db.

body.description: Plain-text bytes. Required and authoritative when storage_location='kms-db'; otherwise an optional backup snapshot. For twins (skill+agent), one body is shared (anti-drift).

capability_resolve.description: Bake-at-serve resolution: load a capability's body and substitute every {{name}} reference with the value its binding resolves to UNDER THE GIVEN SCOPE. scope is a human string ('personal' | 'work') — the same body resolves differently per scope. Bindings resolve to identifiers/paths only, NEVER secrets. Missing bindings fail loud with a required-bindings manifest (error='missing_bindings'), never a silent-empty substitution.

name.description: Capability name to resolve (exact, case-insensitive) — e.g. 'capture'.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

capture.description: Dump a note/content into the knowledge store. Stores the body and creates an artifact. captured_at defaults to now; a caller may declare a different day for its OWN artifact via the optional captured_at, but only for an allowlisted content_subtype ('daily_log' today - the Daily Log twin, #562) and never in the future. Both bounds are refusals, not silent fallbacks (#414).

text.description: The note / content body to store.

title.description: Optional title. Derived from the first line of text if omitted.

source_url.description: Optional URL this note came from (at most 2048 characters).

content_subtype.description: Optional kind of content, e.g. 'transcript', 'conversation', 'note'. Also carries an explicit user-supplied content-type flag ('task' | 'note' | 'reference' | 'quote' | 'person' | 'meeting-note') when the user typed one — pass it through as given, never inferred from the content (capture is dumb; auto-detection is dropped per docs/design/capture-skill-consolidation.md §b). Used downstream to scope what feeds the SOD/EOD state doc (ADR-013).

surface.description: The app/agent/ingest path this capture came through, e.g. 'claude_code', 'gmail_ingest' (open vocab, see vocab.ts SURFACES). Finer than source_channel; used to derive trust and synthesis role at read time (ADR-026, ADR-046 §3). Falls back to the user's default_surface, then to 'api' — never null, since a null surface is a row no role/trust map entry can address (#584). Declare it whenever you know it: the floor is honest, not informative.

trust_override.description: Optional explicit trust tier for THIS capture, overriding the value normally derived from its surface (e.g. a low-trust forward arriving on a trusted surface). One of: perfect|high|medium|low|unverified (ADR-026).

captured_by.description: The actor that captured this (e.g. 'user', or an automation name). Not the surface.

urgency.description: Optional user-supplied urgency dial for THIS capture: 'throw' (fire-and-forget), 'default', or 'file' (the user flagged it as needing fuller downstream handling). Written faithfully and NEVER acted on at capture time — the enrich consumer (#52) reads it to decide how much to do (ADR-018). Set only from an explicit user signal (e.g. a '-throw'/'-file' flag), never inferred from content.

captured_at.description: Optional ISO timestamp (or 'YYYY-MM-DD') declaring the day this content is ABOUT, when that differs from now. Defaults to now. Two hard bounds, both refusals rather than silent fallbacks: a future value is rejected, and it is honoured only for content_subtype in [daily_log] — today just the Daily Log twin (#562), whose day is fixed by the entry it mirrors and is up to seven days before write time when the unattended sweep (#561) writes it. This is a caller DECLARATION about its own artifact, not capture inferring a date; an unbounded dial would let any caller misfile atoms into arbitrary day buckets (#414). See #571 for whether a general originated_at should exist instead.

dedup_key.description: Optional caller-supplied idempotency key (#993), scoped to the caller's user_id, same shape as create_external_link's dedup_key. A second capture with the same dedup_key returns the FIRST artifact's id with deduplicated: true instead of inserting a new row — enforced race-safely by a real unique index, unlike the default content-fingerprint dedup below. Use this when the caller already has a stable identity for what it's submitting (e.g. re-posting the same webhook payload); leave it unset to fall back on the default fingerprint+window guard.

processing_metadata.description: Optional structured processing metadata stored in the processing_metadata column (e.g. { pillars: [...] } on a Daily Log twin, #657).

clean_state_check.description: Evaluate an artifact or recent domain window against the 5-layer Clean State contract (ADR-114): Layer 1 artifact integrity, Layer 2 graph hygiene, Layer 3 task parity, Layer 4 synthesis alignment, and Layer 5 action_ledger health. Read-only; returns per-layer verdicts and remediation steps.

artifact_id.description: Specific artifact UUID to evaluate against Layers 1–5.

domain.description: Domain ('angus' or 'work') to evaluate recent artifacts when artifact_id is omitted.

window_days.description: Lookback window in days for domain or ledger evaluation (default 7).

session_id.description: Optional MCP session ID to scope Layer 5 action_ledger error checks.

client_action_record.description: Record a batch of 1 to 50 client-local UI action runs reported by the browser in-app agent into the append-only action_ledger with seam client_local.

expose.note: Called by the web app's clientActionRecorder to batch client_local audit records (ADR-105 R9, #1558).

action_id.description: The client_local manifest action_id that executed in the browser.

request_id.description: Client-generated UUID for the local execution.

trace_id.description: Optional end-to-end trace_id for the chat turn.

outcome.description: Outcome of the local action execution.

input_keys.description: Sorted top-level keys of the action input (values never leave the browser).

input_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON input.

records.description: Batch of 1 to 50 client-local action execution records.

communication_create.description: Create or file a communication in the appropriate destination per domain and audience register (Meetings database or Investor CRM; Daily Log body for private meetings in the 'angus' domain). Mirrors task_create with lineage (artifact_id, kind='communication') and dedup guards (single_communication, dedup_key). Refuses a private_meeting write to any public destination (ADR-053 §6 amendment).

name.description: The contact's full name. Used as the page title, and as the dedup key when no email is given.

email.description: Email address. The primary dedup key: an existing contact with this email is returned rather than duplicated.

contact_type.description: Validated against the destination's own options before anything is written — read them with notion_database_get. Required by the Work Contacts database.

daily_log_create.description: The dos ritual's Daily Log writer: ONE entry per domain per covered day, holding those days against the ritual. Not for session notes or working logs; record those with capture. `domain` ('work' or 'angus') is required with no default, and so are `date` and `title`. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/daily_log_create.md

domain.description: Required. Which Daily Log to write: 'work' (the Work workspace) or 'angus' (the personal workspace). Each resolves its own database pointer AND its own Notion token — there is no default, because a destination that defaults silently is one that will one day be wrong (ADR-054 §9).

date.description: Required. The day this entry is written for, YYYY-MM-DD. Written to the destination's date property. The duplicate guard keys on the days the entry COVERS (see `covers`), and an entry with no declared covers covers its own date.

covers.description: The days this entry accounts for, YYYY-MM-DD each (#1016): the distinct `captured_at` dates of every atom the dos ritual stamps with this entry's page. Written to the Daily Log property that domain's dos config declares with role 'covers', and the duplicate guard refuses the write when an existing entry already covers one of them. Omitted means [date], a run that closes its own day. Ignored, with a note, when the config declares no Covers property.

pillars.description: The pillar objectives to record for this entry. Written to the Daily Log property that domain's dos config declares with role 'pillars'. Refused if the config declares no property with role 'pillars' (pillars → none declared; write none).

title.description: Required. The entry's title. It is written to whichever property the destination declares as its title property, discovered by introspection — you never name that property.

body.description: The entry's page body, one block per line. '## ' becomes a heading, '- ' / '* ' bullets, '- [ ]' / '- [x]' to-dos, '1. ' numbered items, '> ' quotes; anything else is a paragraph. Inline markdown ([label](url), **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~strikethrough~~) is parsed into Notion rich_text runs. Long lines are split across rich-text runs rather than rejected.

properties.description: Extra Notion property values, keyed by the destination's own property NAME, in real Notion REST shapes — a date is {'date': {'start': '2026-08-21'}}, a checkbox {'checkbox': true}, a select {'select': {'name': 'Daily'}}, a multi-select {'multi_select': [{'name': 'Ops'}]}, rich text {'rich_text': [{'text': {'content': '...'}}]}. These are NOT the claude.ai Notion connector's conventions: no __YES__/__NO__, no 'date:Date:start', no JSON-string arrays. Every name is validated against a live read of the destination before anything is written, and an unknown one is an error listing the valid names.

date_property.description: Which property `date` is written to. Only needed when the destination has zero or more than one date property — with exactly one, it is discovered by introspection.

allow_duplicate.description: Write even though an entry already covers one of these days (#673, #1016). Off by default: the duplicate guard runs whenever that domain's daily_log_data_source_id is configured, and refuses with the existing page's id rather than silently creating a second entry for one day. On refusal, twin_present indicates whether the clashing page has an ahKMS Daily Log twin (#721).

write_twin.description: Also write this entry's ahKMS twin and its `daily_log` pointer, in this call, after the page (#2258): page, then twin, then pointer, returning twin_artifact_id. Off by default, and off means exactly the old behaviour (no twin, no pointer). Pass true only from a ritual that no longer writes the twin itself with capture and external_link_create, or the entry gets two twins. A twin or pointer failure never fails the page: the reply carries a `twin: MISSING` warning instead.

Days bucket on the atom's captured_at, never on when the marker was written, so a late backfill still lands on the day it covers. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/dos_synthesis_coverage.md

from.description: First calendar day of the window, 'YYYY-MM-DD' (UTC). Inclusive. Days are bucketed on the atom's captured_at, so this bounds the days being reported on — not when their markers were written.

domain.description: Whose coverage to report: 'work' (the Work ritual) or 'angus' (the personal one). There is one log PER DOMAIN (ADR-051 §11), so coverage is a per-domain question — a day closed in 'angus' and never in 'work' is covered for the first and uncovered for the second, and a domain-scoped sweep that asks unscoped will skip a genuinely un-run day (#677). This is the dos ritual's routing axis (ADR-051 §1), not the subject-area 'topic' a day's atoms are about. Omitted, markers from every domain are pooled and a day counts as covered if ANY domain closed it — the cross-domain audit view, and exactly what every caller got before this argument existed.

entity_neighbourhood.description: Read the local knowledge graph around one or more entities: resolve a starting set (by id, PARAMPS type, title substring, or properties match), traverse entity↔entity edges up to 2 hops, and return nodes, edges, and per-entity artifact provenance (interactions). This is the closest thing to a 'graph view' read. Use to show what's connected to a person/topic.

entity_id.description: Start from one specific entity. If omitted, the filters below select the starting set.

entity_type.description: Filter the starting set by PARAMPS type, e.g. 'people'.

title_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on starting entities' titles.

properties_match.description: jsonb containment filter on properties, e.g. { profession: 'marketing' } returns people whose properties contain that key/value.

edge_types.description: Restrict entity↔entity edges to these types (ADR-021 vocabulary terms like 'parentOf'/'colleagueOf' or legacy edge types like 'works_with'; matched by equality against stored values). PARA roll-ups/counting (#170): pass ['belongs_to'] to traverse PRIMARY containment only — 'associated_with' is the secondary, NON-COUNTED containment edge and MUST be excluded from any roll-up or count ("show everything under Business" follows belongs_to exclusively; each edge's type field flags which kind it is).

hops.description: Traversal depth over entity↔entity edges (default 1, max 2).

include_archived_edges.description: Include archived (soft-deleted) relationships in traversal. Defaults to false.

include_instance_of.description: ADR-036 §2: opt in to also traverse the virtual 'instance_of' edge from each frontier entity to its vocabulary term-node -- the registry row grounding its entity_type (e.g. an entity_type='people' row -> the term-node for 'people'). Derived from entities.entity_type at query time via the graph_instance_of view; never written per-instance. Default false -- ordinary neighbourhood queries stay clean and cheap. Only this first hop (instance -> term-node) is virtual: once reached, the term-node's own real edges (its exactMatch, a governed_by principle) traverse normally on subsequent hops, giving 'walk from this row to its type, then to the type's governing principle' in one query. Forward direction only -- an entity's own type, never the reverse fan-out of every other instance sharing it.

as_of.description: ISO 8601 instant. When present, restrict traversal to edges valid at that moment (valid_from <= as_of AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > as_of); NULL bounds are open-ended/unbounded), e.g. 'who was my gas supplier in 2026?'. Omit to return all edges regardless of their validity window (current behaviour, unchanged) — as_of is purely opt-in.

limit.description: Max starting entities (default 25).

node_properties.description: Also return every reached node's full `properties` in `nodes` (default false; starting entities always carry theirs). Use when a read has to sort or filter what the traversal reached by its properties, e.g. arrangements by `kind`. Every node carries `archived` either way: a live edge can still reach an archived entity, and the caller decides whether to drop it.

exclude_properties.description: Property keys to omit from returned properties objects on nodes and starting entities (e.g. ['sources', 'notes']).

include_source_notes.description: When node_properties is true, include internal 'sources' and 'notes' properties (default false). These verbose provenance and editorial fields are excluded by default to keep graph traversal payloads within chat context budgets (#1248).

property_keys.description: When node_properties is true, whitelist only these specific keys in returned properties. If omitted, all properties (except excluded ones) are included.

include_entity_edges.description: Include the 'edges' array on each starting entity in 'entities' (default true). Set to false to omit 'edges' on starting entities and avoid repeating edges when 'result.edges' already contains all traversed edges (#1248).

entity_path.description: Find the shortest paths between two entities in the knowledge graph across both edge directions up to max_hops.

entity_promote_edge.description: Reify a binary edge into one or more `arrangement` nodes: create the node, attach per-role participant edges out of it, and link the originating capture. Use when a relationship itself needs properties — a role, a term, a rate — that an edge cannot carry. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/entity_promote_edge.md

edge_id.description: The binary edge to reify (id from entity_relate / entity_neighbourhood). Archived after promotion unless archive_original is false.

kind.description: Arrangement kind, stored in properties.kind — open-vocab (employment | residency | supply | tenancy | …). Reify-by-category and the accumulation counter key on this, NOT entity_type (ADR-035 §2/§4).

title.description: Node title, e.g. 'PM at Acme'. Defaults to the kind if omitted.

valid_from.description: Start of THIS arrangement's window (ISO 8601). For a 1→N split each node carries its own corrected window.

valid_to.description: End of THIS arrangement's window (ISO 8601). Omit if ongoing.

properties.description: Extra node properties; merged under { kind, valid_from, valid_to }.

role.description: Per-role participant edge type OUT of the arrangement (arrangement → participant). Seed roles (open-vocab, ADR-035 §5): employer, employee, resident, at_place, supplier, customer, of_utility. A new kind coins its own roles — unknown values are stored verbatim (soft validation), never rejected or retyped.

participants.description: The per-role edges from this arrangement to each participant (≥1).

Deduplicates on (from, to, relationship_type), so re-running is safe. Prefer the canonical ADR-021 relationship vocabulary. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/entity_relate.md

from_entity_id.description: Source entity id (from upsert_entity or search). Required unless `relationships` is provided.

to_entity_id.description: Target entity id. Required unless `relationships` is provided.

relationship_type.description: Edge type. Prefer the canonical vocabulary — people edges per ADR-021, plus the hierarchy category (broader/narrower, SKOS Areas per ADR-033/#195: broader = child Area -> parent Area) — family: parentOf, childOf, grandparentOf, grandchildOf, ancestorOf, descendantOf, siblingOf, spouseOf, lifePartnerOf, engagedTo; romantic: romanticPartnerOf; social: friendOf, closeFriendOf, acquaintanceOf, neighborOf, livesWith, hasMet, knowsOf, knowsInPassing, knowsByReputation, wouldLikeToKnow, lostContactWith; professional: colleagueOf, worksWith, collaboratesWith, employedBy, employerOf, mentorOf, apprenticeTo, influencedBy; negative: enemyOf, antagonistOf, ambivalentOf; foaf: knows, member, currentProject, pastProject, made; place: livesAt, basedNear, locatedIn; hierarchy: broader, narrower; system: co_occurs_with; other: other. Synonyms auto-map ('mother' → parentOf, 'colleague' → colleagueOf); unknown phrases are stored as 'other' with the raw value preserved in notes (soft validation — capture is never blocked). General-purpose system edge types (legacy + Schema.org spine terms, ADR-033 / #192) also remain valid unchanged: belongs_to, associated_with, related_to, mentions, depends_on, supersedes, knows, works_with, member_of, employed_by, about, located_at, attended, met_at, derived_from, co_occurs_with, engaged_to, married_to, partner_of, vendor_for, client_of, author, is_part_of, has_part, subject_of, was_generated_by, was_attributed_to, references, is_referenced_by, current_project, broader, narrower, skos_related, employer, employee, resident, at_place, supplier, customer, of_utility, knows_about, demonstrates, in_role, student, institution, applicant, applied_to, applied_via, recruiter, hiring_contact. PARA containment (#170): 'belongs_to' is the PRIMARY containment edge — single-parent for project/resource sources (roll-ups/counting traverse it exclusively); 'associated_with' is the SECONDARY, non-counted containment edge (zero or more per entity) for a project/resource's other relevant Areas.

confidence.description: 0.0–1.0 confidence the edge is real (legacy 1 < value <= 100 inputs are automatically divided by 100). Omit if unknown — on an edge that already exists, omitting LEAVES the stored value unchanged (#501; there is no clear-confidence flag, since 'unknown confidence' and 'no opinion supplied this call' are the same thing).

metadata.description: Optional edge attributes, e.g. { context: 'Matheson Lang Gardens' } (the membership # belongs to the provider×property edge, not the provider alone). Omit to leave the edge's stored metadata untouched. When supplied on an edge that already exists, this is a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386, one level deep) against the stored object, NOT a replacement: keys you supply overwrite the same key, keys you don't mention are kept, and a key supplied with value null is DELETED from the stored object. Re-assertion is additive by default — send only the keys you're adding or changing — and deletion stays possible via explicit null (#501 / ADR-035 amendment).

notes.description: Free-text notes on the edge. Omit to leave the caller's previously-recorded prose unchanged on an edge that already exists (#501); pass an empty string to explicitly clear it instead (the exact parallel to metadata's explicit null). Independent of this field: when relationship_type needed normalising (ADR-021), the resulting vocabulary note is re-derived and re-appended on every write. For a recognised synonym (the romantic subtypes — girlfriend, boyfriend, situationship, … — are currently the only note-carrying vocabulary) the note is not caller-erasable: it survives even a later call that supplies new notes or switches to the canonical term. The open-ended 'other' fallback has no such bounded recognition — re-using the SAME unrecognised phrase never duplicates its note, but a call that both switches to a genuinely different unrecognised phrase AND supplies new notes can still lose the earlier phrase, same as any single free-text column would.

valid_from.description: Start of the relationship's validity window (ISO 8601), e.g. when a job or tenancy began. Omit if unknown/unbounded — on an edge that already exists, omitting LEAVES the stored value unchanged (use clear_window to erase it).

valid_to.description: End of the relationship's validity window (ISO 8601), e.g. when a job or tenancy ended. Omit if still active — on an edge that already exists, omitting LEAVES the stored value unchanged (use clear_window to erase it).

clear_window.description: Erase this edge's stored valid_from/valid_to (both set to null). Needed only because omitting the dates now PRESERVES them (#464); pass this to correct a window that should never have been recorded. Cannot be combined with valid_from/valid_to. Defaults to false.

archive.description: Soft-delete this edge instead of creating/updating it live. Archived edges are excluded from entity_neighbourhood and default relationship reads but retained for history. Takes effect before any window logic runs, so combining this with clear_window (or valid_from/valid_to) archives the edge and leaves its stored window untouched — call entity_relate again without archive to change the window. Defaults to false.

overwrite.description: Allow overwriting an existing edge's temporal window with a DIFFERENT one. By default a 2nd same-type edge between the same pair carrying different dates is REFUSED (ADR-035 collision-at-2: overwriting would silently drop the first fact — promote both into an arrangement with entity_promote_edge instead). Set true ONLY to intentionally correct this edge's dates, not to record a 2nd distinct fact. Also gates re-pointing a project/resource's PRIMARY containment parent (#170): a 'belongs_to' write that would give the entity a 2nd primary parent is refused by default; with overwrite: true the old primary edge is archived and the new one written. Defaults to false.

supersedes_relationship_id.description: Optional id of an earlier relationship edge that this edge supersedes (#2053). When supplied on a non-archive write, the superseded edge must exist and belong to you; its valid_to is closed to this edge's valid_from (or the current timestamp when valid_from is omitted) if valid_to is currently null, and metadata cross-links (supersedes_relationship_id on the new edge, superseded_by_relationship_id on the old edge) are recorded.

relationships.description: Optional batch of 1–50 relationships to create, update, or archive in a single call (#1978). Each item runs through full single-edge validation and deduplication.

entity_synthesize.description: Synthesize a concise, factual profile for an entity from evidence in its linked artifacts and update entities.description and properties.synthesis. Supports dry_run (makes LLM call and returns profile without writing back). Uses Gemini by default, with optional Anthropic routing. Returns plain text with LLM output safely quoted.

dry_run.description: If true, runs synthesis without writing back to entity

max_artifacts.description: Maximum linked artifacts to consider (1-10, default 10)

entity_unmerge.description: Reverse an entity merge operation by op_id or loser entity_id. Restores the loser entity (archived=false, clears merged_into), moves repointed relationship edges and artifact links back, un-archives redundant edges, and removes merged-in aliases and carried properties from the winner. Refuses if any affected edge has been edited since the merge.

op_id.description: UUID of the merge operation to reverse (from loser's properties._merge.op_id or system_decisions.decision_payload.mergeOpId).

entity_id.description: UUID of the tombstoned loser entity. If provided without op_id, the merge record is read from this entity.

event_create.description: Create a Google Calendar event. `title` is required. `start` is a full ISO datetime for a timed event or a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day one; `end` is optional and defaults to one hour later, or the next day for all-day. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/event_create.md

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'; 'angus' is this parameter's 'personal'). Which Google account to act as: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

start.description: Event start. Either a full ISO 8601 datetime (e.g. '2026-07-10T14:00:00-07:00' or with a trailing 'Z') for a timed event, or a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD' date for an all-day event.

end.description: Event end. Same format as `start`. If omitted: a timed event defaults to `start` + 1 hour; an all-day event (bare date `start`) defaults to the next calendar day (Calendar's convention for a single-day all-day event — the end date is exclusive).

attendees.description: Optional attendee email addresses to invite.

artifact_id.description: Optional id of the artifact this event came from (e.g. a meeting transcript). Records cross-store lineage so the event is traceable from the knowledge side. When omitted, the event's source is auto-captured from `source_text` (or the title) instead — see `source_text`.

source_text.description: The message that requested this event, used ONLY when no `artifact_id` is given. It is captured as the event's source artifact so every event is traceable back to the thought that produced it (mirrors task_create's #413 treatment) — the request itself IS the source. Pass the user's actual request verbatim (e.g. 'put dentist on the calendar for next Tuesday at 2pm'); if omitted, the title stands in as a thin fallback. The captured artifact carries distinct provenance (content_subtype='event_request') and is excluded from knowledge_search by default (opt in with `include_event_requests`). Ignored when `artifact_id` is supplied (the event already has a source).

single_event.description: Set true when this atom declares exactly ONE event (the common 1:1 case). When true and artifact_id is given, skips creation if ANY kind='event' link already exists for that artifact — prevents eager-Act-at-capture plus a later Act pass from double-creating. Leave false/omitted for the 1:N case (an atom that spawns several distinct events); use dedup_key instead to dedup those individually. WARNING: this is a caller-asserted contract, not a structural one — nothing stops you from passing single_event=true on an atom that actually has several distinct events. Doing so SILENTLY SKIPS every event after the first (only the response text says so; there is no error). If an atom might spawn more than one event, use dedup_key instead, per-event.

dedup_key.description: Stable per-event idempotency key for the 1:N case (e.g. a slug of this specific event's title, when one atom spawns several events). When given with artifact_id, skips creation if a kind='event' link with this exact dedup_key already exists for that artifact; otherwise creates and records it under this key. Mutually exclusive in practice with single_event (single_event is for the 1:1 case; dedup_key is for 1:N). No multi-event orchestration is provided beyond this per-key dedup — the caller still issues one event_create call per event.

external_link_create.description: Record cross-store lineage from an artifact to an external item, or a synthesis marker. A twin must never carry a synthesis marker and an atom must never carry 'consumed_by_state'. 'synthesized' means a human was in the loop; 'synthesized_unattended' does not. They are not interchangeable. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/external_link_create.md

artifact_id.description: UUID of the artifact this link belongs to.

provider.description: External system identifier — e.g. 'internal' for links to other Supabase rows. For Notion, use the WORKSPACE-scoped provider the rest of the system writes ('notion_work' / 'notion_personal'), not a bare 'notion': provider is part of the unique key, so mixing the two fragments an artifact's ledger and a synthesis marker written under the wrong one will not be found by the reads that look for it.

kind.description: What the link represents. Two families, and mixing them up breaks real reads. POINTERS say "this artifact corresponds to that external object": 'task' | 'event' | 'daily_log' (a Daily Log twin pointing at its Notion page, provider the domain's 'notion_work' or 'notion_personal', external_id the page id; #562, ADR-050 §7. Guarded, #2313: refused unless the artifact IS a twin and carries no 'daily_log' pointer naming another page or provider, so the only late write it allows is the pointer attach on a pointerless twin) | 'consumed_by_state' (a Daily Log twin pointing at the State Doc page it was folded into, the SECOND consumption hop, ADR-051 §10 / Erratum 1: artifact_id the TWIN, external_id the State Doc page id, provider the domain's; written by the attended dos session on the owner's approval and by nothing else. Never on an atom: atoms are consumed at hop 1 by a log, and the tool refuses it). SYNTHESIS MARKERS say "this atom went through the Synthesize step": 'synthesized' | 'synthesized_unattended'. For a marker, the kind names the STEP and external_id names the OBJECT (the Daily Log page id). 'synthesized' asserts the human was in the loop, read, corrected, confirmed, and is what an attended ritual writes. 'synthesized_unattended' asserts the opposite: a machine-written draft nobody has confirmed. It is written ONLY by #561's unattended fallback sweep and by nothing else, because the distinction is the whole point, if an attended run wrote it, or the sweep wrote 'synthesized', a swept day would become indistinguishable from a day the owner actually verified (ADR-050 §6, §8). NEVER stamp a synthesis marker on a Daily Log twin: the twin is the ritual's output, not an atom it consumed, and dos_synthesis_coverage buckets markers by the artifact's captured_at, so it would add a phantom count to the very day it reports on. No kind is named 'state_doc', nothing writes one, and the State Doc is a mutable projection that is deliberately NOT twinned (ADR-022/ADR-040, ADR-050 §7). (ADR-013 §7, ADR-018 §5).

external_id.description: External identifier — e.g. a Notion page id for the entry the artifact was folded into.

external_url.description: Optional convenience URL for humans/agents; never required for lookups.

dedup_key.description: Optional pre-creation idempotency key for the 1->many case (e.g. one of several tasks/events spawned from the same atom). Scoped to (artifact_id, provider, kind); see task_create's single_task/dedup_key dedup guard (issue #141).

run_id.description: Run marker obtained by the dos ritual at Step 0. Required when kind='synthesized': ADR-050 §6 defines 'synthesized' as the Synthesize step completing with the human in the loop during the ritual. Callers without a ritual run_id may stamp 'synthesized_unattended' only (#1139).
