state.description: Pull request state filter ('open', 'closed', or 'all'; default 'open').

head.description: Filter pulls by head user or org and branch name in 'user:ref-name' format.

base.description: Filter pulls by base branch name.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return per page (1-100, default 30).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor (next page number as a string).

github_pr_mergeability.description: Read a GitHub pull request's mergeability state in an allowlisted repository using the read-only GitHub token, re-reading once if GitHub has not computed it yet.

github_pr_review_list.description: List reviews on a GitHub pull request with cursor pagination and 2,000-character review body capping.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return per page (1-100, default 30).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor (next page number as a string).

github_pr_update.description: Update the title or body of a GitHub pull request in an allowlisted pr_repos repository, gated by owner approval.

body.description: New pull request markdown body (up to 60,000 characters).

github_repo_get.description: Read a GitHub repository's metadata and default branch in an allowlisted repository using the read-only GitHub token.

github_review_create.description: Post a review on a GitHub pull request in an allowlisted pr_repos repository, gated by owner approval.

body.description: Markdown review body (up to 60,000 characters; required unless event is 'APPROVE').

github_run_job_list.description: List jobs and failed steps for a GitHub Actions workflow run in an allowlisted repository using the read-only token.

limit.description: Maximum number of jobs to return per page (1-100, default 30).

cursor.description: Pagination cursor returned as next_cursor from a previous call.

github_run_list.description: List GitHub Actions workflow runs for a branch or head SHA in an allowlisted repository. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/github_run_list.md

head_sha.description: Filter workflow runs by head commit SHA.

branch.description: Filter workflow runs by branch name.

status.description: Optional workflow run status or conclusion filter.

limit.description: Maximum number of workflow runs to return per page (1-100, default 20).

cursor.description: Pagination cursor returned as next_cursor from a previous call.

gmail_attachment_to_drive.description: Stream an email attachment directly from Gmail to a Google Drive folder server-side without base64 round-tripping through the model context. Resolves the attachment by attachment_id or exact filename and returns the uploaded Drive file metadata.

message_id.description: Gmail message ID containing the attachment.

attachment_id.description: Gmail attachment ID (from gmail_read). Provide attachment_id, attachment_filename, or filename.

attachment_filename.description: Exact attachment filename on the Gmail message when attachment_id is omitted.

filename.description: Alias for attachment_filename: exact attachment filename on the message when attachment_id is omitted.

name.description: Optional target filename for the uploaded Drive file (defaults to the Gmail attachment filename).

drive_filename.description: Alias for name: optional override filename for the uploaded Drive file (defaults to the Gmail attachment filename).

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

gmail_domain.description: Optional Gmail domain override ('work' or 'angus'); defaults to domain or 'work'.

drive_domain.description: Optional Google Drive domain override ('work' or 'angus'); defaults to domain or 'work'.

gmail_draft.description: Compose a draft in a Gmail mailbox, or update an existing one. Does NOT send: it leaves a real draft that can be read, edited in Gmail, sent by hand, or sent with gmail_send_draft. Pass `reply_to_message_id` to reply in-thread. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/gmail_draft.md

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'). Which Google account to send AS: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

to.description: Recipients. Optional ONLY when reply_to_message_id is given, in which case it defaults to that message's sender and the reply goes to them alone. There is no reply-all: name every recipient you want.

subject.description: Subject. Optional only when replying, where it defaults to the original subject with 'Re: ' prefixed.

body.description: Plain-text body. Sent as UTF-8; no HTML.

reply_to_message_id.description: Message id being replied to. Sets In-Reply-To, References and the Gmail threadId, so the reply threads properly in every mail client rather than only in Gmail.

draft_id.description: Update this existing draft instead of creating a new one.

gmail_labels.description: List a mailbox's Gmail labels with their ids, or idempotently create one by name (action='ensure'). Label ids, not names, are what gmail_modify takes.

action.description: 'list' returns every label with its id. 'ensure' creates `name` if missing and returns it either way (idempotent, safe to re-run).

name.description: Label name, required for action='ensure'. e.g. 'meeting_note'.

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'; 'angus' is this parameter's 'personal'). Which Google account to act as: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

gmail_modify.description: Add or remove labels on a Gmail message or thread, mark it read/unread, and archive it or return it to the inbox. Cannot delete: there is no delete tool. Sending is a separate two-step path, gmail_draft then gmail_send_draft.

message_id.description: Message id to modify. Pass message_id / message_ids or thread_id / thread_ids (do not mix message and thread targets).

thread_id.description: Thread id to modify — applies the change to every message in it.

thread_ids.description: Batch thread ids to modify (1..50) — applies the change to every message in each thread.

add_labels.description: Label IDS to add (not names — get ids from gmail_labels). Create a missing label with gmail_labels action='ensure' first.

mark_read.description: true marks read (removes UNREAD); false marks unread (adds UNREAD).

archive.description: true archives (removes INBOX); false moves back to the inbox (adds INBOX). Archiving never deletes — there is no delete tool.

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'; 'angus' is this parameter's 'personal'). Which Google account to act as: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

gmail_priority_triage.description: Run the email pipeline over both Gmail accounts: rules on every thread, a model with graph and State Doc context on uncertain or human mail, then route, hold risky mail for the owner, and cap theirs at 15 a day. mode 'shadow' (default) only logs; 'label' adds ahOS/* labels; 'act' also archives, drafts and files tasks. Notes: docs/guides/tools/gmail_priority_triage.md

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company mailbox) or 'angus' (the personal mailbox). When omitted, falls back to `account` or 'all'.

account.description: Gmail account domain to triage ('personal', 'work', or 'all'). Defaults to 'all'.

mode.description: What the run may do to Gmail. 'shadow' (default): judge and log only, Gmail untouched. 'label': also apply ahOS/* labels (reversible). 'act': also archive what the HITL gate cleared, create reply drafts (never sent) and create confident tasks.

cut_line_priority.description: Priority (1..7) at or above which a thread is routed to the owner and promoted to a Tier-3 artifact. Defaults to 5.

attention_budget.description: Daily target for threads that reach the owner (attention, drafts and review). Defaults to 15.

use_system_2.description: Escalate uncertain and human mail to the System 2 model when one is wired. Defaults to true.

reprocess.description: Re-judge threads an earlier run already decided. Defaults to false.

dry_run.description: When true, computes everything and writes nothing at all: no decision log, no artifacts, no Gmail changes.

max_threads.description: Maximum number of inbox threads to evaluate per account. Defaults to 25.

include_decisions.description: Return the full decision list. Set false for a metrics-only reply.

gmail_read.description: Read one Gmail message, or a whole thread, in full — headers, decoded body text and attachment list. Prefers the plain-text part and keeps link hrefs, so document URLs in transactional mail survive.

message_id.description: Message id to read in full. Exactly one of message_id / thread_id.

thread_id.description: Thread id to read in full — returns every message in the thread, oldest first.

max_chars.description: Truncate each message body to this many characters (default 20000).

max_messages.description: Max messages to return when reading a thread (newest N, default 25).

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'; 'angus' is this parameter's 'personal'). Which Google account to act as: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

gmail_reconcile.description: Reconcile Gmail labels for threads captured into ahOS (issue #356). Applies AhOS on capture, AhOSProcessed on entity sync, and evaluates linked tasks: archives and marks read when no open tasks exist; applies 'Pending Action' if the next move is on Angus; or applies '6: awaiting reply' if waiting on someone else. Supports dry_run preview.

expose.note: http and ui_agent off: it archives threads and marks them read; widening is a separate owner decision (ruling of 21 Nov 2026 on #1338)

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'; 'angus' is this parameter's 'personal'). Which Google account to act as: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

thread_id.description: Specific Gmail thread ID to reconcile. If omitted, reconciles all threads with captured artifacts.

dry_run.description: If true, preview decisions and label changes without modifying Gmail labels or archiving threads.

limit.description: Maximum number of threads to inspect and reconcile in this sweep.

gmail_search.description: Search a Gmail mailbox with Gmail's own query syntax (from:, subject:, newer_than:, label:, is:unread). Returns matching messages with ids, subjects, senders and read/archived state. Use domain='work' for the work.example.com mailbox.

query.description: Gmail search query, in Gmail's own syntax — e.g. `from:noreply@example.com subject:"Notes:" newer_than:7d`. Supports from:, to:, subject:, label:, has:, newer_than:, older_than:, is:unread, and OR / -negation.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor (next_cursor from a previous gmail_search response).

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'; 'angus' is this parameter's 'personal'). Which Google account to act as: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

gmail_send_draft.description: Send an existing draft by id. Irreversible. Cannot compose; every send passes through a mailbox draft first (use gmail_draft to make one), and the sent message is captured. Parks for the owner's approval unless every recipient is one of the owner's own addresses. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/gmail_send_draft.md

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'). Which Google account to send AS: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

draft_id.description: The draft to send, from gmail_draft or from Gmail's own draft list.

gmail_triage_metrics.description: Daily email pipeline metrics for the dashboard: inbox and unread threads, processed, new, needs-attention against the 15-a-day budget, review, drafts, tasks, routes, System 1 versus System 2, and owner corrections. Read-only.

days.description: How many days to return, ending today. Defaults to 14.

attention_budget.description: The daily attention target each day is judged against. Defaults to 15.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone whose midnight cuts the days. Defaults to Europe/London.

gmail_unsubscribe_batch.description: Label a batch of unsubscribe_candidate Gmail threads with ahOS/Unsubscribe and archive them out of the inbox after a single owner approval.

thread_id.description: Gmail thread ID to label ahOS/Unsubscribe and archive.

account.description: Gmail account domain ('personal' or 'work'). Defaults to 'personal'.

domain.description: Optional domain alias ('work' or 'angus'/'personal') when account is omitted.

message_id.description: Optional Gmail message ID on the thread (defaults to thread_id).

sender.description: Optional sender display name or address for audit and approval context.

subject.description: Optional subject line for audit and approval context.

list_unsubscribe.description: Optional List-Unsubscribe header value if available.

decision_id.description: Optional system_decisions row ID associated with the triage decision.

threads.description: Batch of unsubscribe_candidate Gmail thread descriptors to label ahOS/Unsubscribe and archive after owner approval.

dry_run.description: When true, validates the batch without modifying Gmail.

graph_export_rdf.description: Export the knowledge graph's VOCABULARY layer as valid Turtle: the namespace prefixes plus each vocabulary term as a CURIE-compacted triple block. Registry IRIs only — there is no triple store, and it does NOT export instance data such as people, organisations or relationships. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/graph_export_rdf.md

graph_filter.description: Filter the interactive knowledge graph view by search query, entity_types (multi-select), hierarchy_level grouping, or reset filters.

expose.note: Runs in the browser against local UI state; bound via bindLocalHandler in web (ADR-105, #1557).

graph_node_level.description: Move an entity node up or down in hierarchy zoom level (Level 1..14) or set its discrete zoom level in the ahOS knowledge graph.

hot_tier_candidates.description: Return non-hot entities most mentioned in the owner's own captures over a trailing window, ranked to fill the hot tier up to its target size. Read-only. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/hot_tier_candidates.md

decline_quiet_days.description: Days to suppress entities with properties.hot_declined_at (0-365, default 90).

entity_types.description: Entity types to consider (defaults to all types except event, signal, decision, arrangement, domain).

ingest_discover.description: Register a batch of items inventoried from an external system (Notion, Drive, Gmail, ...) as lightweight pointers in the knowledge registry. Records what exists and where it lives WITHOUT pulling in content -- the cheap, frequent layer of Discover & Index. Compose this after listing items from a connector. Idempotent per external id; re-running refreshes changed items.

connector.description: Source system being inventoried, e.g. 'notion', 'gdrive', 'gmail'. Stored as source_channel 'discovered_<connector>'.

external_id.description: Stable id of the item in the source system (the idempotency key).

title.description: Human-readable title of the item. May be null/empty — real source rows often have no title; a title is then synthesised from `summary` or an explicit `(untitled <type>)` placeholder, so the caller does not have to invent one.

summary.description: Short description/summary of the item, if the source exposes one. Used to synthesise a title when `title` is null/empty.

type.description: Source-system item type (e.g. 'Personal Task', 'page'). Used only for the `(untitled <type>)` placeholder when no title/summary is available; falls back to the connector name.

archived.description: Whether the item is archived at the *source* (a `Status: Archived`-style property value, NOT Notion's page-level archive flag). Archived items are excluded from the sweep unless `include_archived` is set.

url.description: Direct link to the item where it lives. Content stays there; we store the pointer.

owner.description: Owner/author in the source system, if known.

owner_email.description: Owner's email in the source system, if known. Tells your files apart from ones shared with you.

mime_type.description: Source-reported MIME type, e.g. 'application/pdf'. A Drive folder ('application/vnd.google-apps.folder') is recorded but never queued for enrichment.

size.description: Size in bytes as the source reports it, if known.

envelope.description: Other source-served envelope fields, copied verbatim (e.g. an email's from/to/subject/date). Facts from the API response only, never text read out of the content (ADR-046 §2).

parents.description: Ids of the item's parent folders/containers in the source system, if known.

source_created_at.description: ISO timestamp the item was created in the source system.

source_modified_at.description: ISO timestamp the item was last modified in the source system.

content_hash.description: Hash/etag of the item's content. Used to detect changes so re-discovery can flag items for re-enrichment.

trashed.description: Whether the item is trashed in the source system (#1212).

items.description: Batch of discovered items to register as pointers (max 200 per call).

include_archived.description: Include items flagged `archived` at the source. Default false: store-by-default, but completed/archived items are opt-in on a sweep (docs/vision.md). Applies to the per-item `archived` property value, not Notion's page-level archive flag.

ingest_drive.description: Ingest a Google Drive file into the knowledge store without taking any Drive-side cleanup action. Downloads/exports the file, persists the artifact with Drive provenance, and returns the routing context so the agent can extract entities and decide keep/move/archive/delete afterward.

file_id.description: Drive file id to ingest into the knowledge store.

title.description: Optional human-friendly artifact title. Defaults to the Drive file name.

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'; 'angus' is this parameter's 'personal'). Which Google account to act as: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

ingest_github.description: Pull the owner's own GitHub activity into the store as artifacts: issues and pull requests they authored or commented on, across every repository the token can see, in a date window. Deliberately not 'involves:', which would turn a record of what they did into a notifications feed. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/ingest_github.md

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) lower bound on last-updated. Defaults to 7 days ago. Re-running an overlapping window is safe: already-ingested items are skipped by URL.

until.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) upper bound on last-updated. Defaults to open-ended.

repo.description: Restrict to one 'owner/name'. Omitted, every repository the token can see, which is the point: the coverage gap is work done in repos you never open a Claude session in.

max_results.description: Max items PER QUERY (default 30). Two queries run, authored and commented, so the ceiling on distinct items is roughly twice this.

dry_run.description: List what WOULD be ingested and write nothing. Worth using first on a wide window: this writes one artifact per item and a busy fortnight is hundreds.

ingest_meeting_notes.description: Chain a detected meeting-note email into one captured atom: fetch its Google Doc, or fall back to the email body, capture it, and link it to the meeting's event entity. No Notion write, no State Doc, no synthesis — this produces the atom and nothing else. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/ingest_meeting_notes.md

message_id.description: Gmail message id to process — the [id] ingest_meeting_notes_detect reported for this meeting-note email.

doc_id.description: Override the Google Doc id to ingest, when the message's own body has none, more than one, or the wrong one. Defaults to the first doc URL matched in the message.

label_name.description: Gmail label marking a processed meeting note (default 'meeting_note', matching scripts/meeting-notes-setup.ts). Doubles as the idempotency check: a message that already carries it is reported and left untouched — nothing is re-captured, re-labelled or re-moved.

target_folder_id.description: Drive folder id to file the doc under once captured. Omit to skip the move step (find or create one with scripts/meeting-notes-setup.ts).

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'; 'angus' is this parameter's 'personal'). Which Google account to act as: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

ingest_meeting_notes_detect.description: Find meeting-note emails in a mailbox using the configured sender/subject detection rules (Google Meet / Gemini today), and report the meeting title and Google Doc links recovered from each. Read-only: label and capture are separate calls. Use domain='work' for the work.example.com mailbox.

newer_than.description: Gmail relative age bound, e.g. '2d', '7d', '1m'. Defaults to '7d'. Keeps a sweep from walking the whole mailbox.

exclude_label.description: Skip messages already carrying this label name, e.g. 'meeting_note'. This is what makes a repeated sweep idempotent.

account.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'; 'angus' is this parameter's 'personal'). Which Google account to act as: personal | work.

domain.description: Which domain to act in: 'work' (the Work company workspace and account) or 'angus' (the personal one).

ingest_slack.description: Pull the owner's OWN Slack messages into the store as artifacts. Scope is 'things I said', never 'things I saw': the filter is from:@me, so a channel's history of other people's writing is never captured. Covers public channels, private ones and DMs the token can see. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/ingest_slack.md

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive. Defaults to 7 days ago. Re-running an overlapping window is safe: already-ingested messages are skipped by permalink.

until.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive. Open-ended if omitted.

channel.description: Restrict to one channel name, without the leading #. Omitted, every conversation the token can reach, INCLUDING DIRECT MESSAGES.

include_dms.description: Whether to ingest direct messages (default true). Set false to take channels only, without changing the token. DMs are captured on their own surface either way, so they stay separable afterwards.

dry_run.description: List what WOULD be ingested and write nothing. Worth running first: this covers DMs by default, and it is better to see the list than to discover it in search results.

instructions_get.description: Fetch the canonical system instructions block (system-instructions) and its staleness / drift status. Copy the returned text into your client system instructions, then run instructions_mark_pasted.

instructions_mark_pasted.description: Record that the canonical system instructions block (system-instructions) was pasted into a non-MCP client surface. Saves the pasted sha256 and timestamp in user_preferences under system_instructions_sync. Defaults to the current canonical hash and now.

sha256.description: The sha256 hash of the system-instructions block pasted into your client system instructions. Defaults to current canonical hash.

pasted_at.description: ISO timestamp when the instructions were pasted. Defaults to now.

integration_list.description: List which external integrations (e.g. Notion tasks, GitHub) are configured for you, with optional provider filtering and redacted non-secret config inspection.

provider.description: Optional provider key (e.g. 'github', 'notion_work') to filter the returned integrations and include its non-secret config in MCP output.

include_config.description: When true, include redacted non-secret config values in the MCP text summary.

integration_set.description: Upsert a user_integrations row for one provider: create it if missing, otherwise MERGE `config` into what is there — keys you do not mention are left untouched, so this never wipes a row. Use when the owner explicitly names a typed integration setting. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/integration_set.md

provider.description: Integration provider key, e.g. 'notion_work', 'notion_personal', 'google_drive', 'google_calendar', 'dex', 'brevo', 'meta_ads', 'linkedin', 'github'. Providers with a known schema are validated on write; unknown providers accept a generic flat config.

config.description: Non-secret config patch (database ids, page ids, workspace names, etc.). MERGED into the existing config — keys you don't mention are left untouched. Do NOT put tokens/secrets here; they belong in env vars (e.g. NOTION_WORK_ACCESS_TOKEN) and are never read from or written to this column.

enabled.description: Toggle the integration on/off. Omit to leave unchanged.

merge_arrays.description: When true, array values in `config` (e.g. github `read_repos`, `issue_repos`, `pr_repos`) are appended to and deduplicated against existing array values instead of replacing them.

job_application_upsert.description: Create or update a job application arrangement node (ADR-120) with its participant edges (applicant, applied_to, applied_via, recruiter, hiring_contact, references CV, belongs_to Job Search), provenance links, and open next-action task. Interactive UI/MCP calls execute directly (refusing with candidates on ambiguous match); unattended worker calls or review-band confidence calls park in the owner Approvals inbox.

id.description: Existing job application arrangement entity id (for explicit updates).

organisation.description: Target organisation name (required when creating if organisation_id is omitted).

organisation_id.description: Existing target organisation entity id for the applied_to edge.

role_title.description: Advertised role title (required when creating a new application).

role_category.description: Role category slug (product, ai_engineering, data_leadership, ops_chief_of_staff, solutions, other). Defaults to 'other' on create.

channel.description: Application channel slug (jumpstart, cord, dex_jobs, jack_and_jill, company_site, recruiter, referral, direct_outreach). Defaults to 'company_site' on create.

ats.description: Optional ATS identifier for company_site applications (e.g. lever, greenhouse, ashby, teamtailor).

stage.description: Canonical ADR-120 stage (identified, matched, drafting, applied, screening, interviewing, offer, accepted, rejected, withdrawn, closed_no_reply). Defaults to 'identified' on create.

applied_on.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601) when submitted; null for pre-application or drafting.

date_precision.description: Date precision indicator (day, month, estimated, unknown).

closed_on.description: ISO date when entering a terminal stage (auto-filled from as_of if omitted on terminal entry).

last_inbound_at.description: ISO timestamp/date of the most recent inbound human reply (resets the 14-day silence clock).

platform_ref.description: External reference code (e.g. UCL B28-00397); highest-priority deduplication key.

salary_expectation_submitted.description: Numeric salary expectation submitted on the application form (private personal finance data).

priority_level.description: ADR-116 7-point priority level (1 = Trivial to 7 = Critical).

source.description: ADR-117 source slug (owner, agent_proposed, email_triage, etc.).

notes.description: Short factual notes on the application.

job_site.description: Job site or agency name for the applied_via edge (e.g. 'Jumpstart', 'Dex jobs').

job_site_id.description: Existing job site or agency organisation entity id for the applied_via edge.

recruiter_ids.description: Optional people entity IDs to link via 'recruiter' edges.

hiring_contact_ids.description: Optional people entity IDs to link via 'hiring_contact' edges.

cv_entity_id.description: Optional tracked CV resource entity id (ADR-098) to link via a 'references' edge (null clears).

area_id.description: Optional Job Search area entity id for 'belongs_to' containment (defaults to resolving 'Job Search').

applicant_entity_id.description: Optional owner self people entity id for the 'applicant' edge (defaults to person_self if present).

evidence_artifact_id.description: Optional provenance artifact id to link via artifact_entity_links and record in stage_history.

stage_note.description: Optional note recorded on the stage_history transition entry.

screening_call_held.description: When entering 'screening', indicates whether the first call has already occurred (controls default next action).

next_action_title.description: Optional explicit title override for the open next-action task.

next_action_due_date.description: Optional explicit due date override (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601) for the open next-action task.

skip_task_sync.description: Set true to skip syncing the open user_tasks row (default false).

as_of.description: Optional ISO date or timestamp used for stage_history and task due-date computation.

reapplication.description: Set true to create a separate re-application node when (organisation, role_title) already exists.

disambiguation_candidates.description: Read-only candidate list attached when unattended ingestion parks an ambiguous match for owner review. Executing without an explicit id (or reapplication: true) refuses rather than creating a duplicate.

confidence.description: Optional dual-axis confidence score (ADR-104). Calls with epistemic in [0.30, 0.85) are parked as action_approval decisions; calls < 0.30 are refused.

epistemic.description: Epistemic truth/identity confidence (0.0-1.0). Calls in [0.30, 0.85) are parked for review; calls < 0.30 are blocked.

job_hunt_gmail_ingest.description: Ingest personal-mailbox ('angus') job application emails (ADR-120 Phase 2): classifies confirmations, rejections, screening invites, digests, task-only alerts, and evidence replies; matches existing applications (platform_ref -> thread_id -> org+role); watermarks per message_id in system_decisions; and gates updates via shadow / label / act modes.

domain.description: Mailbox domain scope. Must be 'angus' (personal mailbox only; 'work' is rejected per ADR-120 §4).

mode.description: Rollout mode: 'shadow' (audit-only watermarks, zero Gmail/approval writes), 'label' (additive ahOS/job-hunt label + Approvals inbox), or 'act' (auto-executes unambiguous updates when auto_apply threshold is enabled and met).

dry_run.description: When true, computes classifications and matches without writing to Supabase or Gmail.

query.description: Optional Gmail search query for inbound/all mail (defaults to 'newer_than:7d').

max_messages.description: Maximum Gmail messages fetched per query (1..500, default 50).

as_of.description: Optional ISO date or timestamp used for stage_history and task due-date computation.

job_list.description: List your background jobs in system_jobs, newest first: pending and processing ones by default, or one status (completed, failed, cancelled). Each row shows type, status, age, attempts, the last error and a short payload summary, never the full payload. Read-only: it cannot cancel or retry a job. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/job_list.md

status.description: List only jobs in this status: pending, processing, completed, failed or cancelled. Omitted, pending and processing jobs are listed.

type.description: List only jobs of this type, which is the queued action id (for example 'entity_derive').

limit.description: Maximum rows to return (1-200, default 50).

job_pipeline_read.description: Read the job search pipeline (ADR-120): loads job application arrangement nodes, participant edges (applied_to, applied_via, recruiter, hiring_contact, applicant, references CV), linked artifacts, and linked user_tasks, then computes 14-day silence flags, 7/14/28/42-day cadence state, last_action_at, and funnel metrics overall, by channel, and by role category.

stage.description: Filter returned applications to one exact stage.

stage_group.description: Filter returned applications by pipeline bucket: all, to_review (identified|matched), drafting, active (non-terminal), submitted, silent (>=14d applied without inbound reply), terminal.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring search over title, organisation, role_title, platform_ref, or notes.

include_closed.description: Include terminal stages (accepted, rejected, withdrawn, closed_no_reply) in returned applications (default true).

as_of.description: Reference ISO date or timestamp for silence/cadence/metrics evaluation (defaults to today UTC).

knowledge_search.description: Search the knowledge store — artifacts and the entity/people graph fused into one ranked list. At least one of `query`, `tags`, `captured_after`, `captured_before` or `not_consumed` must be supplied. Structured filters (`roles`, `tags`, date window, `not_consumed`) apply to the artifact arm only. `tags` (all-of) and `artifacts_only` drop the graph arms. `rank_by_role` ranks a filter-only read by source role. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/knowledge_search.md

query.description: Natural-language or keyword query. Searches artifacts hybrid (full-text + semantic vector, RRF-fused) when the OpenAI embedding key is configured, and falls back to full-text-only when it is not — or when the embedding provider is rate-limited/down, in which case the result is labelled as degraded rather than failing. Optional when structured filters are supplied.

limit.description: Max results (default 10).

captured_after.description: Only include artifacts whose EFFECTIVE date >= this ISO timestamp (e.g. '2026-06-15T00:00:00Z'). Inclusive. Effective date is `originated_at` where the source told us when the content is from, else `captured_at` (ADR-088, #571) — so a 2016 contract enriched today is filtered as 2016, not as today. The parameter keeps the `captured_` name deliberately: renaming it is a real API break for callers already wired to it, and the widened meaning is spelled out here and in the tool description, so nobody is misled by the name alone (same call made for `include_discovered`).

captured_before.description: Only include artifacts whose EFFECTIVE date <= this ISO timestamp. Inclusive. See captured_after for what 'effective' means and why the name still says captured (ADR-088, #571).

not_consumed.description: Exclude artifacts already folded into a daily-log / synthesis entry (i.e. with an artifact_external_links row carrying any synthesis marker kind: 'synthesized' or 'synthesized_unattended'). Used by synthesis consumers like dos-eod to find unconsumed atoms. When not_consumed is true and `roles` is omitted, `roles` defaults to ['narrative'] (ADR-108 §5, ADR-046 §3); pass an explicit `roles` array to override. See ADR-013 §7, ADR-018 §5, ADR-050 §6.

consumed_kinds.description: Which synthesis marker kinds `not_consumed` should treat as consuming. Defaults to ALL of them ('synthesized' and 'synthesized_unattended'), which is what an ordinary day-window read wants. Pass ['synthesized'] to treat only human-confirmed synthesis as consumption, so atoms a machine sweep closed unattended (#561) come back as unconsumed and the day can still be reviewed attended. Ignored unless not_consumed is true. See ADR-050 §6/§8.

domain.description: Whose consumption `not_consumed` should count: 'work' (the Work ritual) or 'angus' (the personal one). Each domain folds atoms into its OWN Daily Log and stamps markers under its own provider, so a domain-scoped ritual must pass its own domain or it treats the other domain's synthesis as its own and skips atoms it never consumed (#677, ADR-051 §11). This is the dos ritual's routing axis (ADR-051 §1) — not the subject-area 'topic' an atom is about. Omitted, no provider predicate is applied at all and EVERY domain's markers count as consumption, which is what a cross-domain audit wants and exactly what every caller got before this argument existed. Ignored unless not_consumed is true.

include_archived.description: Include soft-deleted (archived) artifacts in results. Defaults to false, matching entity_query/person_query. See artifact_delete.

include_task_requests.description: Include task-request provenance artifacts (content_subtype='task_request') in results. These are auto-captured by task_create as the source of an artifact-less task (issue #413) — the message that requested the task. Defaults to false so one-line task requests ('add task: buy milk') don't crowd search results; set true when you specifically want to see them.

include_event_requests.description: Include event-request provenance artifacts (content_subtype='event_request') in results. These are auto-captured by event_create as the source of an artifact-less calendar event (issue #126), mirroring include_task_requests. Defaults to false so one-line event requests don't crowd search results; set true when you specifically want to see them.

include_daily_logs.description: Include Daily Log twins (content_subtype='daily_log') in results. These are the EOD ritual's own output, captured back into the store so a day's synthesis is answerable from the memory side — 'what did I decide on 12 August' (#562, ADR-050 §7). Defaults to false, and that default is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: it is how ADR-051 §9's 'the ritual's own output is never the ritual's input' holds, so tomorrow's day-window read cannot consume today's log and synthesise the synthesis. Set true for exactly the read that wants the synthesis rather than the atoms; never in a day-window/not_consumed synthesis read.

include_scaffolds.description: Include scheduled-task scaffold artifacts (content_subtype='scaffold') in results. These are a Cowork scheduled task's own ritual output, captured back into the store as the INPUT to a later ritual — e.g. friday-reflection-prep's 'Weekly Reflection' scaffold, which dos-reflect reads and archives or consumes (#994, ADR-051 §9). Defaults to false, same load-bearing reasoning as include_daily_logs: it is what keeps an ordinary dos day-window read from surfacing a scaffold as material. Set true only in the read that specifically wants scaffolds, e.g. dos-reflect's own read.

include_reflections.description: Include reflection twins (content_subtype='reflection') in results. These are reflect's own output, captured back into the store alongside the Daily Log entry (#2316). Defaults to false, kept out of day-window reads for the same reason as include_daily_logs and include_scaffolds (ADR-051 §9): the ritual's own output must not come back as an input. Set true only when you specifically want reflections.

include_discovered.description: Include unenriched pointers (lifecycle_stage='discovered' or 'failed' — registered by discover/ingest_enrich_next but never enriched to a body, or enrichment attempted and errored) in day-window/synthesis reads (captured_after/captured_before/not_consumed). Defaults to false: these rows have nothing to narrate, so a connector backfill of hundreds of bare pointers doesn't drown the day's real atoms (issue #567). Does not affect a bare query with no structured filters — that always surfaces discovered/failed pointers by title (ADR-016's 'what I have' search; ADR-046 §3). Set true to audit the discover backlog, e.g. to see what a flood landed or what ingest_enrich_next needs to retry — there is no dedicated list_by_stage tool yet.

rank_by_role.description: Rank a filter-only read (no `query`) by ADR-046 §3 source role BEFORE the limit is taken: every `narrative` row first, then `evidence`, `metrics`, `excluded`; within a role, newest effective date first (the same `effective_at` the window filters on, ADR-088). A row's role is resolved from the owner's surface→role map exactly as artifact_get's `role=` reports it. The ranking covers the WHOLE matching set, not the returned page, and drops robot-authored rows from non-excluded tiers (use `roles` to filter membership explicitly). The response opens with each role's count. Defaults to false (newest effective date first, role ignored). Built for the dos ritual's bounded backlog slice (ADR-067 §3, #911). Refused alongside `query`, whose order is relevance.

roles.description: Filter artifacts by effective ADR-046 §3 synthesis role ('narrative', 'evidence', 'metrics', 'excluded'). Honors surface_role_map, role:<role> tag overrides, and robot-authored exclusion (unless 'excluded' is included or 'not_robot_authored' is set). Defaults to ['narrative'] when `not_consumed` is true and `roles` is omitted (ADR-108 §5); pass an explicit array to override.

tags.description: Only artifacts carrying ALL of these tags (exact, case-sensitive match on the artifact's tags, e.g. ['doc:cv', 'golden']). Applied inside the search itself, before its row ceiling: the full-text arm filters before its cap, and the semantic arm ranks the tagged artifacts themselves by exact distance, so a tagged match is never crowded out by untagged ones. Skips the entity and people arms, which have no artifact tags. May be the only filter: with no `query` it lists the tagged artifacts newest first.

artifacts_only.description: Skip the entity and people arms: return artifacts only. Defaults to false. Use it for document-shaped queries (a document name, a filename), where name-matching entities and people otherwise fill the top of the list. Changes nothing on a filter-only read, which is artifacts-only already.

ledger_query.description: Query the append-only action_ledger by time window, action_id, caller, client_id, session_id, request_id, trace_id, parent_request_id, or outcome. Returns matching rows (enriched with OAuth client_name; rows record only input_keys and input_sha256, never input values) or a summary of counts by action and outcome with row_estimate and total_bytes.

mode.description: Query mode: 'rows' returns matching ledger rows; 'summary' returns counts by action and outcome plus table size.

since.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at (ISO 8601 datetime).

until.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at (ISO 8601 datetime).

caller.description: Filter to a specific caller surface (e.g. 'mcp', 'http', 'ui', 'worker').

client_id.description: Filter to a specific OAuth client_id.

trace_id.description: Filter to a specific end-to-end trace_id.

outcome.description: Filter to a specific audit outcome.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return in 'rows' mode (1..500, default 100).

link_create.description: Create one or many artifact-entity links.

links.description: One or many artifact-entity links to create.

link_delete.description: Delete one artifact-entity link by id.

id.description: Link id.

link_get.description: Read one artifact-entity link by id.

id.description: Link id.

link_query.description: Read artifact-entity links with optional artifact, entity, or link_type filters.

limit.description: Max rows to return (default 20).

link_upsert.description: Create or update one or many artifact-entity links using the unique artifact/entity/link_type key. On an existing link, omitted optional fields (confidence_score, created_by, notes) are left unchanged.

links.description: One or many artifact-entity links to upsert.

mark_artifact_derived.description: When true, stamps processing_metadata.derivation = { status: 'completed', derived_at, attempts: 1, provider: 'interactive' } on each distinct artifact_id in links via set_artifact_derivation (#1978).

linkedin_post.description: Publish a LinkedIn member post. Uses the native LinkedIn Posts API (routing='native' on the user_integrations 'linkedin' row, authenticated via LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN). Posts are public-by-config; pass visibility to override per call. Parks for the owner's approval on every agent call.

text.description: The post body (commentary). LinkedIn allows up to 3000 characters.

visibility.description: Override the visibility configured for this integration, for this post only.

image_base64.description: Optional base64-encoded image bytes (with or without a data:image/...;base64, prefix) to upload via LinkedIn Images API and attach to the post.

image_content_type.description: Optional MIME type for image_base64 (defaults to image/png).

image_alt_text.description: Optional accessibility alt text for the attached image (up to 4086 characters).

mcp_result_probe.description: Diagnostic probe with no side effects for checking what an MCP client shows the model (text content, structured result, or both).

nonce.description: Caller-chosen nonce (1-64 characters) used to derive deterministic probe markers.

meeting_create.description: File a meeting in either workspace with its time, type, internal attendees and external contacts. Every convention is checked against the live database schema first: an unknown Type option, an unresolvable attendee name, or a value the database has nowhere to put all fail before anything is written.

domain.description: Which workspace: 'work' (Meetings) or 'angus' (Meeting Notes). Required, no default — each is a separate Notion integration.

title.description: Meeting title. Sentence case, descriptive and concise.

start.description: Start as an ISO 8601 datetime, e.g. 2026-09-15T10:15:00+01:00. Include the offset; a bare date loses the time.

end.description: End as an ISO 8601 datetime. Written as the date property's end.

type.description: Validated against the destination's own Type options before anything is written — read them with notion_database_get rather than guessing.

attendees.description: Internal attendees, as Notion user ids or exact display names. Names are resolved against the workspace's user list; an unknown or ambiguous name is an error, never a dropped attendee.

external.description: External attendees, as existing contact page ids or objects like {"name":"Ada Lovelace","email":"ada@example.com"}. Objects are resolved through the same dedup as contact_create, so an existing contact is reused rather than duplicated.

body.description: Meeting notes as Markdown — headings, bullets, paragraphs.

source_url.description: Link to the calendar event or call.

date_property.description: Name the date property explicitly, for a database with more than one.

meta_ads_call_tool.description: Invoke a Meta Ads tool by name (list_ad_accounts, list_campaigns, list_adsets, list_ads, get_insights). Use meta_ads_list_tools to discover tool names and their input schemas. All tools are read-only Marketing API GETs; there is no way to pause, edit or create an ad through this tool.

name.description: Meta Ads tool name, exactly as returned by meta_ads_list_tools.

arguments.description: Arguments for the tool, matching its inputSchema from meta_ads_list_tools.

meta_ads_list_tools.description: Discover the read-only Meta Ads tools available (ad account/campaign/ad-set/ad listing, spend/impressions/clicks insights). Returns each tool's name, description, and JSON-schema input. Call this first, then invoke a tool with meta_ads_call_tool. Requires a Meta system-user access token scoped ads_read (META_ADS_ACCESS_TOKEN). Read-only: there is no write tool in this catalog, by design (#646) — pausing, editing or creating ads is out of scope.

notion_block_delete.description: Delete a block from a Notion page by block_id. The block is moved to the page's trash, so it can be restored from the Notion UI. Refuses blocks belonging to the State Doc (ADR-053 one-writer rule) by walking up to the containing page first.

domain.description: Required. Which workspace: 'work' (the Work workspace) or 'angus' (the personal one). No default — the workspaces are separate Notion integrations with disjoint page access (ADR-054 §9).

block_id.description: The block to delete: a 32-hex Notion id (dashed or undashed) or a Notion URL. Read block ids from notion_page_get.

notion_comment_create.description: Create a comment on a Notion page or block, or reply to an existing discussion thread. In Notion, comments can either start a new top-level thread on a page or block (via parent: { page_id } or parent: { block_id }), or reply to an existing thread (via discussion_id). Exactly one destination must be specified.

domain.description: Required. Which workspace: 'work' (the Work workspace) or 'angus' (the personal one). No default — the workspaces are separate Notion integrations with disjoint page access (ADR-054 §9).

page_id.description: The page to comment on: a 32-hex Notion id or URL. Starts a new top-level comment thread on the page. Exactly one of page_id / block_id / discussion_id.

block_id.description: The block to attach a comment to: a 32-hex Notion id or URL. Starts a new comment thread on that block. Exactly one of page_id / block_id / discussion_id.

discussion_id.description: The discussion thread to reply to: a 32-hex Notion discussion id. Adds a reply to that existing thread. Exactly one of page_id / block_id / discussion_id.

text.description: The comment body text. Converted into Notion rich text runs. Provide either text or rich_text.

rich_text.description: Raw Notion rich_text array if providing formatted rich text directly. Provide either text or rich_text.

notion_comment_list.description: List comments on a Notion page or block: top-level comments and open discussion threads. In Notion, pages are blocks, so passing a page_id or block_id lists comments attached to that object.

domain.description: Required. Which workspace: 'work' (the Work workspace) or 'angus' (the personal one). No default — the workspaces are separate Notion integrations with disjoint page access (ADR-054 §9).

block_id.description: The page or block whose comments to list: a 32-hex Notion id (dashed or undashed) or a Notion URL. Pages in Notion are blocks, so a page id lists page-level comments.

page_id.description: Alias for block_id. The page whose comments to list.

limit.description: Number of comments to return (default 50, max 100).

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous call, to fetch the following page of comments.

notion_completed_at_stamp.description: Evaluates a Notion page.properties_updated webhook event against the completed_at_stamp automation rule and stamps or clears the Completed at property when status changes.

expose.note: Dispatched internally by the /webhooks/notion receiver after HMAC verification (ADR-104 L1, ADR-105 L4)

notion_config_get.description: Return the owner's persisted Notion integration config(s) from user_integrations. Pass provider='notion_work' or provider='notion_personal' to get one workspace; omit to get both. notion_work holds Work workspace config (tasks DB, dos-hl pointers). notion_personal holds personal workspace config (tasks, people, meeting notes DBs). IDs are non-secret but user-specific — fetch at runtime rather than hard-coding.

provider.description: Which Notion workspace to return. Omit to return both (notion_work + notion_personal).

notion_database_get.description: Read a Notion database's schema: every property name, type, and the options of each select, multi_select and status. This is how you find out what notion_page_create will accept, for any database rather than only the tasks one.

domain.description: Which workspace: 'work' (work) or 'angus' (personal). Required, no default — each is a separate Notion integration and sees only its own databases.

database_id.description: The database to introspect. Exactly one of database_id / data_source_id.

data_source_id.description: A data source id; resolved to its parent database first. The *_data_source_id notion_config_get prints.

notion_database_query.description: List a Notion database's rows with flattened property values — the list-shaped read, where notion_search finds by title and notion_page_get reads one page. `domain` ('work' or 'angus') is REQUIRED, no default: separate integrations, each token seeing only its own workspace. Cursor-paginated. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/notion_database_query.md

domain.description: Required. Which workspace the database lives in: 'work' (the Work workspace) or 'angus' (the personal one). No default: the two are separate Notion integrations with disjoint access (ADR-054 §9), and a data source missing from one may be sitting in the other.

data_source_id.description: The data source to query: a 32-hex Notion id (dashed or not) or a full URL carrying one. This is the READ half of a database under Notion's 2025-09-03 API, the id notion_config_get prints for every *_data_source_id key (tasks_source_data_source_id, meetings_source_data_source_id, daily_log_data_source_id, ...). A *_database_id is the container and is refused by Notion here.

filter.description: Notion's own filter object, passed through untouched. One condition: {"property":"Status","status":{"does_not_equal":"Done"}}. Compound: {"and":[{...},{...}]} / {"or":[...]}. Property names are the database's exact names; the value shape depends on the property type (status, select, multi_select, date, checkbox, people, relation, rich_text, title, number). An invalid filter comes back as Notion's validation error, verbatim.

sorts.description: Notion's own sorts array, passed through: [{"property":"Due date","direction":"ascending"}] or [{"timestamp":"last_edited_time","direction":"descending"}]. Applied in order.

properties.description: Property NAMES to show per row, in this order. Omitted, every property is rendered. The title property is always the row heading and is never repeated as a column, so leave it out of this list. Narrow this on wide databases: a Tasks DB with twelve properties and a hundred rows is a lot of text nobody reads.

limit.description: Rows per call (default 50, max 100, Notion's own page cap). More rows come back as a next_cursor, never as a silent cut.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous call, to fetch the following page of rows.

notion_page_create.description: Create a page in either Notion workspace: a row in a database, or a child page under a page. `properties` are Notion's own REST shapes, validated against the database schema before anything is written — an unknown select option is refused here because Notion would silently create it instead. State Doc and Daily Log refused: they have their own writers.

domain.description: Which workspace: 'work' (work) or 'angus' (personal). Required, no default — each is a separate Notion integration and sees only its own pages.

database_id.description: Create a row in this database. The *_database_id notion_config_get prints. Exactly one of database_id / data_source_id / parent_page_id.

data_source_id.description: Create a row in the database behind this data source. The *_data_source_id notion_config_get prints; it is resolved to its database first.

parent_page_id.description: Create a child page under this ordinary page. Accepts an id or a Notion URL. A page parent has no schema, so only the title applies.

title.description: The page title. Written into whichever property the database declares as its title.

properties.description: Other properties, keyed by the property NAME, in Notion's own REST shapes — e.g. {"Event time": {"date": {"start": "2026-09-14T10:00:00Z"}}, "Type": {"select": {"name": "General"}}}. Validated against the schema before anything is written. Ignored for a page parent.

body.description: Page body as Markdown — headings, bullets, paragraphs. Rendered to blocks, one per line, so it is not subject to Notion's 2000-character single-run cap.

icon.description: A single emoji for the page icon.

notion_page_get.description: Read any Notion page or block container: its properties, then every child block with id, type, and Markdown-formatted text (preserving inline links and rich-text annotations). `domain` ('work' or 'angus') is REQUIRED, no default -- the workspaces are separate integrations with disjoint page access. Read-only. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/notion_page_get.md

domain.description: Required. Which workspace to read from: 'work' (the Work workspace) or 'angus' (the personal one). No default — the workspaces are separate Notion integrations with disjoint page access (ADR-054 §9), and a page that 404s in one may live in the other.

page_id.description: The page to read: a 32-hex Notion id (dashed or not) or a full notion.so / app.notion.com URL. A BLOCK id is also accepted — pass a has_children block's id back in to list its nested children.

max_blocks.description: Max blocks to return in one call (default 300, max 1000). Further blocks come back via next_cursor.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous notion_page_get call, to fetch the following page of blocks.

notion_page_update.description: Write to any Notion page — the write half of the page surface. `domain` ('work' or 'angus') is REQUIRED, no default. Ops: 'append' blocks, 'update_block' to rewrite one block in place, 'update_properties' — which also sets `icon` and trashes or restores the page via `archived`. Refuses State Doc pages. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/notion_page_update.md

domain.description: Required. Which workspace to write to: 'work' (the Work workspace) or 'angus' (the personal one). No default — each domain resolves its own token, and a destination that defaults silently is one that will one day be wrong (ADR-054 §9; #820).

op.description: Required. append: add blocks to the end of a page (or after `after`). update_block: replace ONE block's text in place, keeping its type. update_properties: patch page properties with raw Notion REST value shapes.

page_id.description: append / update_properties: the target page — a 32-hex id (dashed or not) or a full Notion URL. append also accepts a block id as the parent.

after.description: append: place the new blocks immediately after this sibling block id (from notion_page_get) instead of at the end.

body.description: append: the content, one block per line. '- ' / '* ' become bullets, '- [ ]' / '- [x]' to-dos, '1. ' numbered items, '> ' quotes, '#'/'##'/'###' headings; anything else is a paragraph. Inline markdown ([label](url), **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~strikethrough~~) is parsed into Notion rich_text runs.

block_id.description: update_block: the block to rewrite. Get ids from notion_page_get.

block_type.description: update_block: the block's type exactly as notion_page_get reported it (paragraph, bulleted_list_item, heading_2, to_do, …). Required because Notion's block PATCH is keyed by type.

text.description: update_block: the block's new text (supports inline markdown links [label](url) and **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~strikethrough~~). Replaces THAT block's rich text wholesale; neighbouring blocks are untouched.

checked.description: update_block on a to_do block: set the checkbox state in the same call.

properties.description: update_properties: keyed by property NAME with real Notion REST value shapes — {"select": {"name": "Green"}}, {"date": {"start": "2026-08-23"}}, {"checkbox": true} — not the claude.ai connector's __YES__ / "date:X:start" conventions.

archived.description: update_properties: true moves the page to Notion's TRASH, false restores it. Recoverable either way — Notion's API has no permanent delete — so there is no confirm gate. Properties are untouched by both. May be combined with `properties` in one call.

icon.description: update_properties: the page icon, in Notion's raw shape — {"emoji": "📓"} or {"external": {"url": "https://…"}}. Same raw-REST convention as `properties`.

notion_search.description: Find a page or database by TITLE in either Notion workspace — the discovery half, since notion_page_get and notion_page_update both need an id. `domain` ('work' or 'angus') is REQUIRED, no default. Titles only: Notion's search does not index block text. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/notion_search.md

domain.description: Required. Which workspace to search: 'work' (the Work workspace) or 'angus' (the personal one). No default — the two are separate Notion integrations that each see only their own workspace (ADR-054 §9), so a page missing from one may be sitting in the other.

query.description: Words to match against page and database TITLES. Notion's search does not index block text, so a phrase that appears INSIDE a page will not find it — search for what the page is called. Omit to list the most recently edited objects instead.

type.description: Restrict results to pages or to databases. Omit for both.

limit.description: Max results to return (default 25, max 100).

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous call, to fetch the following page of results.

notion_user_list.description: List the people and bots in one Notion workspace with their ids, for filling a person-typed property. Read these rather than reusing an id from a skill body: a stale id assigns real work to nobody, and says nothing when it does.

domain.description: Which workspace: 'work' (work) or 'angus' (personal). Required, no default — each is a separate Notion integration with its own members.

onedrive_audit_vs_gdrive.description: Walk a personal OneDrive folder tree and a Google Drive folder tree, classifying files into matched, only_in_onedrive, only_in_gdrive, size_or_hash_mismatch, and counter_copy_candidates.

onedrive_folder_id.description: OneDrive folder item ID to audit (defaults to 'root' when onedrive_path is omitted).

onedrive_path.description: OneDrive folder path relative to root (for example '/Backup - Google Drive'). Ignored when onedrive_folder_id is provided.

gdrive_folder_id.description: Google Drive folder ID to compare against.

domain.description: Google Drive domain ('work' or 'angus'; default 'angus').

recursive.description: Whether to recursively walk subfolders in both trees (default true).

planning_edit.description: Edit the Work planning document by applying patch, upsert and remove ops to named collections. All ops land or none do, and they apply server-side against whatever is current, so a concurrent human edit is not overwritten wholesale. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/planning_edit.md

ops.description: Changes to apply, all or none. Three shapes: {collection, op:'patch', id, value} merges value into the record with that id and FAILS if there is none, so a typo'd id cannot create a half-formed record; {collection, op:'upsert', value} replaces the whole record or appends it when the id is new, and value must carry a string `id`; {collection, op:'remove', id} deletes it. Writable collections are roadmapItems, modelIssues, modelDecisions, modelQuestions and risks — run planning_read first to confirm, since the API is the authority. The goal tree, domain registries, periods, people and budget are NOT writable and are refused by name: they are structure and change in code.

label.description: Label for the snapshot this write creates, shown in the page's Load panel. Say what changed and that an agent did it, e.g. 'mcp: close landing-page issue'.

baseSnapshotId.description: The snapshot id you read before composing these ops. Supply it whenever you read and then think before writing: if someone saved in between, the write is refused with a 409 naming the current snapshot instead of silently overwriting their edit. Omit only when reading and writing in one uninterrupted step.

planning_read.description: Read the Work planning document — roadmap, issues, decisions, open questions and risks. Call it with NO arguments first: that returns the snapshot id, a row count per collection, and the collection names, which is what you need before asking for any one of them. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/planning_read.md

collections.description: Collections to return in full, e.g. ['modelIssues','modelQuestions']. OMIT THIS ON THE FIRST CALL: with no collections the tool returns an index (snapshot id, and a row count per collection) plus the list of writable collections, which is how you find out what exists without pulling ~90KB of document into context. Ask for collections by name once you know which you need.

posthog_connections.description: List the configured PostHog connections with their project id, region and test-account filter policy. Each connection is a separate PostHog project with its own contract, so their numbers are NOT comparable and must never be summed. A connection whose filter policy is UNDECLARED refuses reads until a policy is set.

posthog_project_filter.description: Read a PostHog project's own 'filter out internal and test users' setting, live from PostHog. This is the authoritative content of the test-account contract (#742); it is deliberately not copied into this repo, so use this rather than assuming what it contains.

connection.description: Connection slug, e.g. 'work' (the row provider is 'posthog:<slug>').

posthog_query.description: Run one read query against a single PostHog connection and return the rows stamped with connection, project, region, filter policy and pull time. Refuses (never silently rewrites) a HogQL query that omits the {filters} placeholder when the connection requires filtering, because PostHog would otherwise return unfiltered numbers that look correct. One connection per call by design: cross-connection totals are meaningless.

connection.description: Connection slug, e.g. 'work'. Run posthog_connections to list them.

query.description: A PostHog query object, passed through verbatim. For raw SQL use {kind:'HogQLQuery', query:'...'}. IMPORTANT: when the connection's filter policy is 'required', a HogQL query MUST include the literal `{filters}` placeholder in its WHERE clause (e.g. `... where timestamp >= now() - interval 7 day and {filters}`) AND pass `filters: {filterTestAccounts: true}` alongside it. Without both, PostHog silently returns unfiltered numbers that look correct — measured at 18% high on 7-day event volume for project 110015. Structured query kinds (TrendsQuery etc.) set `filterTestAccounts: true` directly instead. There is no debugging bypass on this tool — for a declared debugging read that needs unfiltered traffic, use posthog_query_debug instead, which always returns filtered and unfiltered together rather than the unfiltered figure alone. In HogQL, event properties are read as `properties.<name>` (including `$`-prefixed properties like `properties.$lib` and `properties.$os`, never bare `$lib`), and person properties as `person.properties.<name>`.

posthog_query_debug.description: Run one guarded query twice against a 'required'-policy connection — as given, and with only filterTestAccounts flipped to false — and render total, filtered and difference together. The unfiltered number is never emitted alone. Requires a `reason`, carried into the stamp. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/posthog_query_debug.md

connection.description: Connection slug, e.g. 'work'. Must declare filter_policy 'required'.

query.description: The SAME guarded query shape posthog_query requires: for HogQL, the {filters} placeholder in the SQL plus filters:{filterTestAccounts:true}; structured kinds set filterTestAccounts:true directly. Pass exactly ONE query — this tool derives the unfiltered leg itself by flipping filterTestAccounts to false on the identical query text, it does not accept two.

reason.description: Why this debugging read needs unfiltered traffic, e.g. 'reproducing the scroll-to-end crash, which was hit on a test account'. Required: this tool exists for a declared debugging purpose, not a general bypass of filter_policy, and the reason is carried into the stamp so that purpose travels with the numbers.

posthog_write.description: Make one authenticated write against a PostHog connection (POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE on an /api/ path). Travels on a SEPARATE write credential, so reads keep a key that cannot mutate anything. Refuses unless the connection declares write_policy 'allowed'; cohort and project-filter edits need acknowledging, because they restate history. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/posthog_write.md

connection.description: Connection slug, e.g. 'work'. Must declare write_policy 'allowed'.

method.description: HTTP method. DELETE additionally requires acknowledge_destructive.

path.description: PostHog API path, starting '/api/'. When it names a project (/api/projects/<id>/...) that id must match the connection's project, so a stamped result always describes the project it claims. Example: '/api/projects/110015/cohorts/225061/'.

body.description: JSON request body, passed through verbatim. Omit for DELETE.

acknowledge_retroactive.description: Required for cohort and project-filter edits. Those are applied at QUERY time to all history, so saving one restates every past number rather than only changing what happens next. Set true only when that is understood and intended.

acknowledge_destructive.description: Required for DELETE. There is no undo.

domain.description: Required. Which Google account: 'work' (work) or 'angus' (personal). No default (ADR-054 §9).

spreadsheet_id.description: Bare spreadsheet id or a docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id> URL.

sheets_write.description: Write cell values to a Google Sheet (`domain` required, no default). `mode`: update writes `values` at `range` (null leaves a cell as it is); append adds rows below the table at `range`; clear empties `range`, keeping formatting. Values are stored as given (RAW) unless `value_input_option: 'USER_ENTERED'`. Returns ranges and counts, never values.

domain.description: Required. Which Google account: 'work' (work) or 'angus' (personal). No default (ADR-054 §9).

spreadsheet_id.description: Bare spreadsheet id or a docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id> URL.

mode.description: Write mode: 'update' writes values at range, 'append' adds rows below the table at range, 'clear' empties values in range (keeping formatting).

range.description: A1 range, required in every mode. For 'append' it names the table to append below, e.g. "'Log'!A:D".

values.description: 2D array of cell values (string, number, boolean, or null) for 'update' and 'append'. null leaves that cell as it is (Google skips nulls); "" sets it empty. Omit for 'clear'.

value_input_option.description: RAW stores what you send, so '=SUM(A1)' stays text. USER_ENTERED parses as if typed in the UI: formulas run (IMPORTXML, IMAGE and IMPORTDATA fetch external URLs) and '1/2' may become a date. Pass it only for a formula you mean.

domain.description: Required. Which State Doc to write: 'work' (the Work workspace) or 'angus' (the personal workspace). Each resolves its own page pointer AND its own Notion token — there is no default, because a destination that defaults silently is one that will one day be wrong (ADR-054 §9).

op.description: Required. replace: rewrite a section's body, keeping its heading. rename: rewrite the heading (and optionally the body) in one call. insert: add a new section at an explicit anchor. delete: remove a section entirely.

heading.description: replace | rename | delete: the EXACT heading text of the section to act on, copied verbatim from the page. Zero matches or more than one is an error, never a guess.

new_heading.description: rename: the heading text to write. insert: the heading of the new section. Must not duplicate a heading already on the page.

body.description: The section's new body, one block per line. '- ' / '* ' become bullets, '- [ ]' / '- [x]' to-dos, '1. ' numbered items, '> ' quotes; anything else is a paragraph. Inline markdown ([label](url), **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~strikethrough~~) is parsed into Notion rich_text runs. Required for replace; optional for rename and insert; rejected for delete.

after_heading.description: insert anchor: place the new section after the whole section with this exact heading.

before_heading.description: insert anchor: place the new section immediately before the section with this exact heading.

at_end.description: insert anchor: place the new section at the end of the page.

heading_level.description: insert only: heading level for the new section. Defaults to 2.

Every other read tool returns a human-summarised projection, never a raw row, so this is the only way to discover a column through ahkms. Reads the live database, so it cannot drift. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/store_schema.md

table.description: Table or view to describe, e.g. 'artifacts', 'entities', 'people'. Omitted, every table and view PostgREST exposes is listed by name with its column count — call again with one of those names for its columns. An unknown name is an error that lists what does exist rather than an empty result.

Guarded against matching open Tasks-DB tasks. WARNING: `single_task` on an atom holding several tasks silently skips after the first. Full notes: docs/guides/tools/task_create.md
