workspace.description: Deprecated, use `domain` ('work' | 'angus'). Which Notion workspace's tasks database to write to: 'notion_work' or 'notion_personal'.

notes.description: Optional details, added as the task's body.

due.description: Optional due date (YYYY-MM-DD). Only applied if a 'due' property is mapped in the Notion integration config. Triage default (issue #298): when omitted and a 'due' property IS mapped, defaults to tomorrow — pass an explicit date (stated or inferred from the request) to override; the response says when the default was applied.

for_person_id.description: Optional person entity id (from entities/people) representing the person this task is a promise or commitment to (#1028). Writes the Notion relation to the person's page where the target database has one (or via property_map.for_person), and always records an artifact_entity_links row linking the task's source artifact to this person with link_type 'related' and notes 'promise_to' so the graph knows.

artifact_id.description: Optional id of the artifact this task came from (e.g. a meeting transcript). Records cross-store lineage so the task is traceable from the knowledge side. When omitted, the task's source is auto-captured from `source_text` (or the title) instead — see `source_text`.

source_text.description: The message that requested this task, used ONLY when no `artifact_id` is given. It is captured as the task's source artifact so every task is traceable back to the thought that produced it (issue #413) — the request itself IS the source. Pass the user's actual request verbatim (e.g. 'add a task to call the dentist tomorrow'); if omitted, the title stands in as a thin fallback. The captured artifact carries distinct provenance (content_subtype='task_request') and is excluded from knowledge_search by default, so one-line task requests don't crowd search. Ignored when `artifact_id` is supplied (the task already has a source).

single_task.description: Set true when this atom declares exactly ONE task (the common 1:1 case — e.g. a later Act pass, such as EOD synthesis, re-visiting an atom eager Act may already have created a task from). When true and artifact_id is given, skips creation if ANY kind='task' link already exists for that artifact — prevents eager-Act-at-capture plus a later Act pass from double-creating. Leave false/omitted for the 1:N case (an atom that spawns several distinct tasks); use dedup_key instead to dedup those individually. WARNING: this is a caller-asserted contract, not a structural one — nothing stops you from passing single_task=true on an atom that actually has several distinct tasks. Doing so SILENTLY SKIPS every task after the first (only the response text says so; there is no error). If an atom might spawn more than one task, use dedup_key instead, per-task.

dedup_key.description: Stable per-task idempotency key for the 1:N case (e.g. a slug of this specific task's title, when one atom spawns several tasks). When given with artifact_id, skips creation if a kind='task' link with this exact dedup_key already exists for that artifact; otherwise creates and records it under this key. Mutually exclusive in practice with single_task (single_task is for the 1:1 case; dedup_key is for 1:N).

skip_notion_dedup.description: Opt out of the Tasks-DB duplicate guard (issue #734). By default (false/omitted) task_create reads the target Tasks database itself — the system of record — for an OPEN task whose title matches this one (exact, case-insensitive, trimmed) or whose configured relation property already points at the same source page (properties.relation, when given). A match is reported as a duplicate and NOTHING is created, unlike single_task/dedup_key (which only guard against the lineage ledger, `artifact_external_links` — a check that misses a task entered straight into Notion, or an ambiguous Notion failure that actually landed a page; see ADR-040's erratum, #413). Pass true when you deliberately want a second task despite a same-titled one existing (e.g. a genuinely recurring task) — this also skips the extra Notion read the guard costs, so the unguarded fast path pays nothing for it.

properties.description: Rich Notion properties beyond title/due/notes (issue #145 gap 2). Each field maps through the integration's property_map (abstract name -> Notion property NAME) and is validated against the target database's actual schema via introspection (retrieve_database_schema) — an unmapped or nonexistent property, or an invalid select/multi_select/status option, throws a clear error rather than an opaque Notion 400. Omit entirely to skip the extra schema-introspection API call (fast path, unchanged from before this field existed).

status.description: Task status (single-select or Notion 'status' type — e.g. 'Not started', 'In progress', 'Done'). Mapped via the integration's property_map (abstract key 'status'); the value must be one of the target property's configured options — an invalid option throws an error listing the valid ones.

priority.description: Task priority (single-select — e.g. 'Low', 'High'). Mapped via property_map's 'priority' key; value must match one of the configured options. Triage default (issue #298): when omitted, defaults to the top priority tier (first of 'High'/'P1'/'P0' the DB accepts, per ADR-040 §3) — pass an explicit value (stated or inferred from the request) to override; the response says when the default was applied.

priority_tier.description: Normalized priority tier (1, 2 or 3, where 1 is the top tier per ADR-040 §3's Normalised Priority). Resolved against the target Tasks database's live Priority options (tier 1 tries '1 High', 'High', 'P1', 'P0'; tier 2 tries '2 Medium', 'Medium', 'P2'; tier 3 tries '3 Low', 'Low', 'P3', 'P4'); refuses before any write if no option matches. Cannot be combined with properties.priority.

priority_level.description: Canonical 7-point task priority level (1 = Trivial lowest to 7 = Critical highest; ADR-116). Resolved against the target Tasks database's live Priority options (levels 5..7 resolve to High tier options; levels 3..4 resolve to Medium tier options; levels 1..2 resolve to Low tier options). Cannot be combined with properties.priority or properties.priority_tier.

domain.description: Task domain/area (single-select — e.g. 'Product and Engineering'). Mapped via property_map's 'domain' key; value must match one of the configured options.

estimates.description: Size/effort estimate (single-select — e.g. 'S', 'M', 'L'). Mapped via property_map's 'estimates' key; value must match one of the configured options.

type.description: Task type(s) (multi-select — e.g. ['Task', 'Polish']). Mapped via property_map's 'type' key; every value must match one of the configured options.

tags.description: Free-form tags (multi-select — e.g. ['launch-v1.0.0', 'Mobile']). Mapped via property_map's 'tags' key; every value must match one of the configured options.

owner.description: Notion person id to set as the task owner (people property, mapped via property_map's 'owner' key). If omitted, defaults to the integration config's notion_user_id ('assign to me unless clearly someone else') when that config value is set; if the config has no notion_user_id, owner is left unset rather than invented.

relation.description: Link this task back to a source Notion page (e.g. a meeting note) via a relation property. The property NAME is resolved through property_map using relation.property as the abstract key; the value(s) are page ids you already have.

property.description: Abstract property key to map via property_map (e.g. 'relation') to the Notion relation property's NAME on the tasks database.

page_ids.description: Notion page id(s) to link, e.g. the source meeting note. These are Notion page ids the caller already has — this tool does not resolve artifact_id to a Notion page id.

confidence.description: Optional dual-axis confidence score (ADR-104). Calls with epistemic in [0.30, 0.85) are parked as action_approval decisions; calls < 0.30 are refused.

epistemic.description: Epistemic truth/identity confidence (0.0-1.0). Calls in [0.30, 0.85) are parked for review; calls < 0.30 are blocked.

task_crud.description: Create, query, get, update, complete, delete, or bulk-delete actionable user tasks in ahOS.

operation.description: The task management operation to perform.

id.description: Task ID for get, update, complete, or delete.

status.description: Task lifecycle status filter or value (proposed, someday, todo, in_progress, blocked, done, cancelled; ADR-117).

priority_level.description: Canonical 7-point task priority level filter or value (1 = Trivial lowest to 7 = Critical highest; ADR-116).

task_type.description: Task cadence and type filter or value (one_off, recurring, habit, milestone; ADR-117).

recurrence_rule.description: Optional schedule or RRULE string when task_type is recurring or habit (ADR-117).

effort.description: Execution effort size filter or value (quick, small, medium, large; ADR-117).

energy_mode.description: Execution or cognitive mode filter or value (deep_work, admin, waiting_on, quick_win; ADR-117).

source.description: Provenance filter or value (owner, agent_proposed, email_triage, meeting_sweep, ritual; ADR-117).

due_before.description: Filter tasks due before this timestamp.

due_after.description: Filter tasks due after this timestamp.

query.description: Search term matching task title or notes.

patch.description: Fields to update during an update operation.

status.description: Task lifecycle status slug (proposed, someday, todo, in_progress, blocked, done, cancelled; default: todo; ADR-117).

priority_level.description: Canonical 7-point task priority level (1 = Trivial lowest to 7 = Critical highest; ADR-116).

task_type.description: Canonical task cadence and type slug (one_off, recurring, habit, milestone; default: one_off; ADR-117).

recurrence_rule.description: Optional schedule or RRULE string when task_type is recurring or habit (ADR-117).

effort.description: Optional execution effort size slug (quick, small, medium, large; ADR-117).

energy_mode.description: Optional execution or cognitive mode slug (deep_work, admin, waiting_on, quick_win; ADR-117).

source.description: Optional provenance slug recording how the task entered ahOS (owner, agent_proposed, email_triage, meeting_sweep, ritual; ADR-117).

due_date.description: Task due date in ISO 8601 format.

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default: 20).

view_screen.description: Inspect the user's current screen, active workspace tab, graph selection, and filters. Call this tool before acting on 'this' or 'the selected' entity or edge to understand what the user is looking at. Set include_record to true to fetch the full database record of the selected entity.

expose.note: Runs in the browser against local UI state; bound via bindLocalHandler in web (ADR-105, #1557).

include_record.description: Whether to hydrate the full database record of the currently selected entity

weekly_kpi_snapshot.description: Compute and optionally persist the KMS Weekly Scorecard across Cloud Drives (OneDrive Personal, Google Drive 'angus' and 'work') and ahOS knowledge-management pillars (Knowledge & Capture, Tasks & Governance, System & Action Ledger) under dedup_key 'kpi_weekly:<YYYY-Www>' (surface 'kpi_snapshot', role 'metrics'). Distinct from the Work company scorecard on work-mcp (scorecard_*).

window_days.description: Lookback window in days for weekly velocity and health metrics (default 7, max 90).

include_drives.description: When true (default), query OneDrive Personal and Google Drive (angus + work) quota, top-level folders, duplicate confidence bands, and parity highlights.

include_system_doctor.description: When true (default false), run ahos_doctor checks and include the verdict in system_and_ledger.

record_snapshot.description: When true (default), persist or update the weekly scorecard artifact in ahKMS under dedup_key 'kpi_weekly:<YYYY-Www>' with surface 'kpi_snapshot' (role 'metrics'). Set false for dry-run inspection.

week_key.description: Optional ISO week key override (e.g. '2026-W44'). Defaults to the current UTC ISO week.

whatsapp_ingest.description: Ingest synced WhatsApp messages into ahKMS grouped into one daily transcript artifact per `(chatJid, YYYY-MM-DD)`. Deduplicates on `whatsapp:<chatJid>:<YYYY-MM-DD>`, updates existing daily transcripts in-place when late messages arrive, and splits 1:1/self-chats (`whatsapp_dm`) from group chats (`whatsapp`) so ADR-046 §3 role policies can govern them independently.

chat_jid.description: Optional chat JID or chat name substring to ingest from. Omit to sweep across all allowed chats.

query.description: Optional keyword filter so only matching daily chat transcripts are ingested.

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO timestamp lower bound. Defaults to 7 days ago. Re-running an overlapping window is safe: daily transcripts deduplicate on `whatsapp:<chatJid>:<YYYY-MM-DD>` and update in-place when new messages arrive later that day.

until.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO timestamp upper bound. Defaults to open-ended.

from_me_only.description: When true, ingest only (chat, day) transcripts where the owner sent at least 1 message (`fromMe: true`), preserving the full day's replies in those participated chats. Defaults to `user_integrations.whatsapp.config.ingest_from_me_only` if configured, else false when `chat_jid` is specified or true on a whole-store sweep.

max_results.description: Maximum daily chat transcripts to ingest in this sweep (default 100, max 500).

dry_run.description: List what WOULD be ingested without writing any artifacts.

sync.description: When true, run a short Baileys companion sync before sweeping messages.

whatsapp_list_chats.description: List synced WhatsApp chats (1:1 DMs, group chats, and self-chat) ordered by most recent message, with optional name/JID and kind filters.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on chat name or JID.

kind.description: Filter by chat kind: 'dm' (1:1), 'group', 'self' (Message Yourself), or 'broadcast'.

limit.description: Max chats to return, ordered by most recent message first (default 50, max 200).

sync.description: When true, run a short Baileys companion sync before reading the chat list.

whatsapp_read_messages.description: Read or search synced WhatsApp messages across one chat or all chats, filtered by date window, sender direction, or keyword.

chat_jid.description: Chat JID (e.g. '447700900000@s.whatsapp.net' or '1203630...@g.us') or case-insensitive chat name substring. Omit to search across all synced chats.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring search over message text, sender name, or chat name.

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO timestamp lower bound (inclusive).

until.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO timestamp upper bound (inclusive).

from_me.description: When true, return only messages sent by you; when false, only incoming messages; omit for both.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return, chronological within the matched window (default 50, max 500).

sync.description: When true, run a short Baileys companion sync before reading messages.

whatsapp_status.description: Inspect the linked WhatsApp companion device status, local store path, synced chat/message counts, and last sync timestamp.

sync.description: When true and a linked Baileys auth session is present, perform a short live sync against WhatsApp Web before returning status.
